Proposition 6.14.11 . 1A99E612D41C Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with Kähler form $\omega $, let $W\subset X$ be a closed submanifold of positive codimension, and let $\pi \colon Y	o X$ be the blowup of $X$ along $W$, with exceptional divisor $E=\pi ^{-1}(W)$. Then $Y$ is a compact complex manifold, and there are a smooth function $ho \colon X	o [0,\infty )$ with $ho ^{-1}(0)=W$ and a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta $ on $Y$ with $\eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log (ho \circ \pi )$ on $Y\setminus E$, such that $\pi ^*\omega +\varepsilon \eta $ is a Kähler form on $Y$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon >0$. The form $\eta $ is the curvature of a smooth quadratic Hermitian metric on the line bundle $\mathcal O_ Y(-E)$, whose local frames are the function $1$ on $Y\setminus E$ and the local equations of $E$ near $E$. In particular $Y$ is a compact Kähler manifold. Consequently every log resolution of a coherent ideal on $X$, as above, is a compact Kähler manifold. Proof. By proposition 9.6.3 , $Y$ is a complex manifold and $E$ is a smooth hypersurface with $\mathcal I_ W\mathcal O_ Y=\mathcal O_ Y(-E)$; moreover $Y$ is compact, since $\pi $ is proper (proposition 9.6.2 ), and $\pi $ restricts to a biholomorphism $Y\setminus E	o X\setminus W$. The last assertion follows from the preceding ones by induction: since $X$ is compact, a log resolution is a composite of finitely many blowups along closed submanifolds of positive codimension, and each intermediate manifold is compact Kähler by what precedes. We construct $\eta $ as the curvature of a metric on $\mathcal O_ Y(-E)$ and show that it is positive definite along the fibers of $E	o W$ (Step 1). Since $\pi ^*\omega $ is positive in the remaining directions, $\pi ^*\omega +\varepsilon \eta $ is then positive definite near $E$ for small $\varepsilon >0$ (Step 2), and also away from $E$ (Step 3). We use the charts of proposition 9.6.3 . Near a point of $W$ at which $W$ has codimension $r$, choose coordinates $(z,w)$ on $X$, $w=(w_1,\ldots ,w_ r)$, with $W=\{ w=0\} $. For each pivot $i$ the blowup has a chart with coordinates $(z,t,v)$, $v=(v_ j)_{j
eq i}$, in which \[  \pi (z,t,v)=(z,t	ilde v),\qquad 	ilde v_ i=1,\quad 	ilde v_ j=v_ j\  (j
eq i);  \] in it $E=\{ t=0\} $, and the fibers of $E	o W$ are the sets $\{ z=	ext{const},\  t=0\} $. If $r=1$ there is no variable $v$, and $\pi $ is the identity near the point. Step 1: a closed $(1,1)$-form that is positive along the fibers of $E$. Choose finitely many charts $V_1,\ldots ,V_ N$ of $X$ covering $W$, with coordinates $(z^\alpha ,w^\alpha )$ such that $W\cap V_\alpha =\{ w^\alpha =0\} $, and put $V_0=X\setminus W$. Grouping the members of a partition of unity subordinate to this cover (proposition 5.2.6 ) according to a set $V_\alpha $ containing their supports, we obtain a smooth partition of unity $(\lambda _\alpha )_{0\leq \alpha \leq N}$ on $X$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\lambda _\alpha \subset V_\alpha $. Put \[  ho =\lambda _0+\sum _{\alpha =1}^ N\lambda _\alpha |w^\alpha |^2,  \] each term extended by zero outside $V_\alpha $. This is a smooth nonnegative function on $X$ that vanishes on $W$, because $\lambda _0=0$ there, and is positive on $X\setminus W$: at a point $x
otin W$ some $\lambda _\alpha (x)$ is positive, and $w^\alpha (x)
eq 0$ if $\alpha \geq 1$. We describe $ho $ near a point $x_0\in W$, in coordinates $(z,w)$ as above on a polydisc $\Delta $ centered at $x_0$. Shrinking $\Delta $, we may assume that $\Delta $ does not meet $\operatorname{Supp}\lambda _0$, nor $\operatorname{Supp}\lambda _\alpha $ for the indices $\alpha $ with $x_0
otin V_\alpha $, and that $\Delta \subset V_\alpha $ for the others. For such an $\alpha $, each component $w^\alpha _ k$ vanishes on $W=\{ w=0\} $, so \[  w^\alpha _ k(z,w)=\sum _{l=1}^ rw_ l\int _0^1 rac{\partial w^\alpha _ k}{\partial w_ l}(z,sw)\, \mathrm ds,  \] that is, $w^\alpha =A_\alpha w$ with a holomorphic $r	imes r$ matrix $A_\alpha $ on $\Delta $. At points of $W$ the matrix $A_\alpha (z,0)=(\partial w^\alpha _ k/\partial w_ l)(z,0)$ is invertible: since $w^\alpha $ vanishes on $W$, its derivatives in the $z$-directions vanish there, and the Jacobian matrix of the coordinate change $(z,w)\mapsto (z^\alpha ,w^\alpha )$ is invertible. Hence, on $\Delta $, \[  ho =\sum _\alpha \lambda _\alpha |A_\alpha w|^2=w^*\mathcal Q\, w,\qquad \mathcal Q=\sum _\alpha \lambda _\alpha A_\alpha ^*A_\alpha ,  \] where the sums run over the indices $\alpha \geq 1$ with $x_0\in V_\alpha $, and $w^*$ is the conjugate transpose of the column vector $w$. The Hermitian matrix $\mathcal Q$ is smooth and positive semidefinite, and it is positive definite at $x_0$, because the coefficients $\lambda _\alpha (x_0)$ of the invertible matrices $A_\alpha (x_0)$ add up to one; shrinking $\Delta $, we may assume that $\mathcal Q$ is positive definite on $\Delta $. In a chart $(z,t,v)$ over $\Delta $ we obtain \[  ho \circ \pi =|t|^2h_ E,\qquad h_ E(z,t,v)=	ilde v^*\mathcal Q(z,t	ilde v)\, 	ilde v,  \] and $h_ E$ is smooth and positive, since $	ilde v
eq 0$. Define a real $(1,1)$-form $\eta $ on $Y$ by $\eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log (ho \circ \pi )$ on $Y\setminus E$ and $\eta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log h_ E$ on each chart $(z,t,v)$ as above. These definitions agree. Off $E$ we have $\log (ho \circ \pi )=\log |t|^2+\log h_ E$, and $\log |t|^2$ is pluriharmonic there. On the overlap of two charts, the local equations $t$ and $t'$ of $E$ generate the same ideal $\mathcal O_ Y(-E)$, so $t'=ut$ with $u$ holomorphic and nowhere zero. Off $E$ the corresponding functions $h_ E$ and $h'_ E$ satisfy $\log h_ E-\log h'_ E=\log |u|^2$. Both sides are continuous on the overlap and $E$ is nowhere dense, so this identity holds on the whole overlap, and $\log |u|^2$ is pluriharmonic. Thus $\eta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $Y$. It is the curvature, in the sense of definition 6.14.9 , of the metric on the line bundle $\mathcal O_ Y(-E)$ with the frame $1$ on $Y\setminus E$, the frames $t$ on the charts and the transition functions $t$ and $t'/t$, for which $|1|^2=1/(ho \circ \pi )$ and $|t|^2=1/h_ E$. These squared norms are smooth and positive, and they satisfy the compatibility condition of that definition because $ho \circ \pi =|t|^2h_ E$ and $h'_ E=|t/t'|^2h_ E$. We show that $\eta $ is positive definite along the fibers of $E	o W$. Fix a point $(z_0,0,v_0)$ of $E$ in a chart, and put $\mathcal Q_0=\mathcal Q(z_0,0)$. On the fiber $\{ z=z_0,\  t=0\} $ we have $h_ E=	ilde v^*\mathcal Q_0	ilde v$. Write $\mathcal Q_0=\Gamma ^*\Gamma $ with an invertible matrix $\Gamma $, for instance the positive square root of $\mathcal Q_0$, and let $e_1,\ldots ,e_ r$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb C^ r$. Then $h_ E=|F(v)|^2$ on the fiber, where $F(v)=\Gamma 	ilde v=\Gamma e_ i+\sum _{j
eq i}v_ j\Gamma e_ j$ is an affine map whose linear part $\Lambda \xi =\sum _{j
eq i}\xi _ j\Gamma e_ j$ is injective, and $F(v)$ never lies in the image of $\Lambda $, because the columns $\Gamma e_1,\ldots ,\Gamma e_ r$ are linearly independent. Writing $\langle a,bangle =\sum _ ka_ k ar b_ k$ on $\mathbb C^ r$, we have $\partial _{ ar v_ l}|F|^2=\langle F,\Gamma e_ langle $ and $\partial _{v_ k}|F|^2=\langle \Gamma e_ k,Fangle $, so for $\xi \in \mathbb C^{r-1}$ \[  \sum _{k,l
eq i} rac{\partial ^2\log |F|^2}{\partial v_ k\partial  ar v_ l}\, \xi _ k ar\xi _ l = rac{|\Lambda \xi |^2}{|F|^2}- rac{|\langle \Lambda \xi ,Fangle |^2}{|F|^4} = rac{|F|^2|\Lambda \xi |^2-|\langle \Lambda \xi ,Fangle |^2}{|F|^4}.  \] By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality this is nonnegative, and it vanishes only if $\Lambda \xi =\mu F$ for some $\mu \in \mathbb C$. Since $F$ does not lie in the image of $\Lambda $, this forces $\mu =0$, so $\Lambda \xi =0$ and $\xi =0$. By the matrix criterion, the restriction of $\eta $ to each fiber of $E	o W$ is positive definite. Step 2: positivity near $E$. The form $P=\pi ^*\omega $ is a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form on $Y$. We regard the real $(1,1)$-forms $P$ and $\eta $ in a chart $(z,t,v)$ as Hermitian forms on holomorphic tangent vectors, given by their coefficient matrices, so that $P(	au ,	au )=\omega (\mathrm d\pi \, 	au ,\mathrm d\pi \, 	au )$ by the chain rule; norms of tangent vectors are taken in the coordinates of the chart. Let $V$ be spanned by the vectors $\partial /\partial v_ k$ and $H$ by the vectors $\partial /\partial z_ l$ and $\partial /\partial t$, and write $P$ and $\eta $ in block form with respect to the decomposition of the tangent space into $V$ and $H$. At points of $E$ we have $\mathrm d\pi (\partial /\partial v_ k)=t\, \partial /\partial w_ k=0$, while $\mathrm d\pi (\partial /\partial z_ l)=\partial /\partial z_ l$ and $\mathrm d\pi (\partial /\partial t)=\sum _ j	ilde v_ j\, \partial /\partial w_ j$ are linearly independent. Since $\omega $ is positive definite, $P_{HV}=0$ and $P_{HH}$ is positive definite at points of $E$, while $\eta _{VV}$ is positive definite there by Step 1. Choose finitely many compact sets $K_\iota $ whose interiors cover $E$, each contained in a chart $(z,t,v)$. The smallest eigenvalues of $P_{HH}$ and of $\eta _{VV}$ are continuous and positive on the compact sets $E\cap K_\iota $, so there are $a,c>0$ such that they exceed $2c$ and $2a$, respectively, on $E\cap K_\iota $ for every $\iota $. Let $M>0$ bound the operator norm of $\eta $ on every $K_\iota $, so that $|\eta (	au ,	au ')|\leq M|	au ||	au '|$, and choose $\ell \in (0,1]$ with $2M\ell +M\ell ^2\leq a/2$. Where $P_{HH}$ is invertible, the linear map $L=P_{HH}^{-1}P_{HV}\colon V	o H$ depends continuously on the point, and it vanishes on $E$. Hence every point of $E\cap K_\iota $ has a neighborhood on whose intersection with $K_\iota $ we have $P_{HH}\geq c$, $\eta _{VV}\geq a$ and $\| L\| \leq \ell $. Let $O_\iota $ be the union of these neighborhoods. Then \[  \mathcal N=\operatorname{Int}\Bigl ( igcup _\iota K_\iota \Bigr )\cap  igcap _\iota  igl (O_\iota \cup (Y\setminus K_\iota ) igr )  \] is an open neighborhood of $E$ with $\mathcal N\cap K_\iota \subset O_\iota $ for every $\iota $. On $\mathcal N\cap K_\iota $ we have, for $\xi \in V$, \[  \eta (\xi -L\xi ,\xi -L\xi )\geq  igl (a-2M\| L\| -M\| L\| ^2 igr )|\xi |^2\geq  rac a2|\xi |^2,\qquad |\xi -L\xi |\leq 2|\xi |.  \] Write a tangent vector at a point of $\mathcal N\cap K_\iota $ as $	au =\xi +\zeta $ with $\xi \in V$ and $\zeta \in H$, and put $\sigma =\zeta +L\xi \in H$. Completing the square, \[  P(	au ,	au )=P_{HH}(\sigma ,\sigma )+S(\xi ,\xi ),\qquad S=P_{VV}-P_{VH}P_{HH}^{-1}P_{HV},  \] and $S\geq 0$ because $P\geq 0$ (take $\zeta =-L\xi $, so that $\sigma =0$). Hence $P(	au ,	au )\geq c|\sigma |^2$. Since $	au =(\xi -L\xi )+\sigma $, \[  \eta (	au ,	au )\geq  rac a2|\xi |^2-4M|\xi ||\sigma |-M|\sigma |^2.  \] Therefore, for $\varepsilon >0$, \[  (P+\varepsilon \eta )(	au ,	au )\geq (c-\varepsilon M)|\sigma |^2+ rac{\varepsilon a}2|\xi |^2-4\varepsilon M|\xi ||\sigma |.  \] The right-hand side is a quadratic form in $(|\sigma |,|\xi |)$, which is positive definite as soon as $\varepsilon M<c$ and $(c-\varepsilon M)a>8\varepsilon M^2$; and $(\sigma ,\xi )
eq 0$ for $	au 
eq 0$. Thus $\pi ^*\omega +\varepsilon \eta $ is positive definite on the fixed neighborhood $\mathcal N$ of $E$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon >0$. Step 3: positivity away from $E$. On the compact set $Y\setminus \mathcal N\subset Y\setminus E$ the map $\pi $ is a local biholomorphism, so $\pi ^*\omega $ is positive definite at every point. Cover $Y\setminus \mathcal N$ by finitely many compact sets contained in charts. On each of them the smallest eigenvalue of the coefficient matrix of $\pi ^*\omega $ is bounded below by a positive constant $c'$, and the operator norm of the coefficient matrix of $\eta $ is bounded by a constant $M'$, with $c'$ and $M'$ independent of the set. Hence $\pi ^*\omega +\varepsilon \eta $ is positive definite on $Y\setminus \mathcal N$ if $\varepsilon M'<c'$. Together with Step 2, this shows that $\pi ^*\omega +\varepsilon \eta $ is positive definite on all of $Y$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon >0$. It is closed, since both terms are, so it is a Kähler form on $Y$. $\square$

text: Definition 6.14.12 . 4E814A4EB7D1 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold. A quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi $ on $X$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(c,\mathfrak a)$ if it has analytic singularities of type $(c,\mathfrak a)$, the function $\exp (\varphi /c)$ is smooth on $X$, including at its zeros, and on every log resolution $\pi $ of $\mathfrak a$, with $\pi ^*\mathfrak a=\mathcal O(-D)$, one has locally \[  \varphi \circ \pi =c\log |s_ D|^2+h,\qquad h\text{ smooth}.  \]

In this section $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, is a bounded pseudoconvex open set, $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and integrals are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure unless another measure is specified. For an integer $m\geq 1$ we put \[  H_ m=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| _ m^2 =\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad K_ m(z)=\sup _{\| F\| _ m\leq 1}|F(z)|^2.  \] Thus $H_ m$ is the space $\mathcal H_{mu}(\Omega )$ of theorem 6.8.9 , for the complex manifold $\Omega $ and the weight $mu$, and the function $K_ m$ is the Bergman kernel of $H_ m$ on the diagonal. We need that $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space of holomorphic functions that generates the multiplier ideal $\mathcal I(mu)$, with bounded coefficients near each point. These facts were proved in section 6.6 on bounded pseudoconvex open sets, also for measures $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ comparable with Lebesgue measure (theorem 6.8.9 , lemma 6.8.10 ), and the next lemma restates them in the notation of this section. Throughout this section, $\varrho $ denotes a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Such measures arise in section 6.16 , where the kernels are computed with the volume form of a Kähler form. Lemma 6.15.1 . C2732E72E566 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, be a bounded pseudoconvex open set, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and let $\varrho $ be a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Put \[  \mathcal H=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| ^2=\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad \langle F,Gangle =\int _\Omega F ar G\, \mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV.  \] For every compact set $K\subset \Omega $ there is a constant $C_ K$ such that $|F(z)|\leq C_ K\| F\| $ for all $F\in \mathcal H$ and $z\in K$. The space $\mathcal H$ is a separable Hilbert space, and it has an orthonormal basis, that is, an orthonormal family $(e_\ell )$, finite or countable, whose linear span is dense. For every such family and every $F\in \mathcal H$, the partial sums of $\sum _\ell \langle F,e_\ell angle e_\ell $ converge to $F$ in norm and locally uniformly on $\Omega $, and $\sum _\ell |\langle F,e_\ell angle |^2=\| F\| ^2$. The germs of the elements of $\mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ at every point of $\Omega $, and near each point finitely many elements of $\mathcal H$ already generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$. Let $x\in \Omega $, and let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s\in \mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then there are a neighborhood $V$ of $x$ and a constant $C$ such that every $F\in \mathcal H$ can be written as $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ with $h_ i\in \mathcal O(V)$ and $\sup _ V|h_ i|\leq C\| F\| $. Proof. We regard $\Omega $ as a complex manifold, with the single chart given by the identity map. Then $\psi $ is a weight on $\Omega $ in the sense of section 6.8 , the set $\Omega $ satisfies the hypotheses of theorem 6.8.9 , and $\mathcal H$ is the space $\mathcal H_\psi (\Omega ,\varrho )$ of that theorem, with the same inner product. Hence (1) is contained in theorem 6.8.9 (1) and (2), and (2) follows from theorem 6.8.9 (3), because an initial segment of an enumerated orthonormal basis is a finite family of elements of $\mathcal H$. Finally, (3) is the first assertion of lemma 6.8.10 , applied to the weight $\psi $ on $\Omega $. $\square$ By lemma 6.15.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$ and $\varrho =1$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space on which evaluation at each point is a bounded linear functional; in particular $K_ m$ is finite. Let $(e_\ell )$ be an orthonormal basis of $H_ m$. Then 2D48BBAB29E1 6.15.2  egin{equation}  K_ m=\sum _\ell |e_\ell |^2. \end{equation} Indeed, let $F$ lie in the unit ball of $H_ m$ and put $c_\ell =\langle F,e_\ell angle $. By lemma 6.15.1 (1), $F(z)=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell (z)$ and $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2=\| F\| _ m^2\leq 1$, so the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|F(z)|^2\leq \sum _\ell |e_\ell (z)|^2$. Conversely, for each $N$ the function $F_ N=\sum _{\ell \leq N}\overline{e_\ell (z)}e_\ell $ satisfies $F_ N(z)=\| F_ N\| _ m^2=\sum _{\ell \leq N}|e_\ell (z)|^2$; if this number is positive, then $F_ N/\| F_ N\| _ m$ lies in the unit ball, and $\sum _{\ell \leq N}|e_\ell (z)|^2=|F_ N(z)|^2/\| F_ N\| _ m^2\leq K_ m(z)$. The same argument applies to the kernel of the space defined with $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in place of Lebesgue measure, for an orthonormal basis of that space. Lemma 6.15.3 . 09CBB2B6BA0F The function $K_ m$ is real analytic on $\Omega $. Near each point of $\Omega $ it is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, where $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ are finitely many generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$ near that point. If $\pi \colon Y	o \Omega $ is a holomorphic map from a complex manifold $Y$ such that $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)=\mathcal O_ Y(-D)$ for an effective divisor $D$ on $Y$, for instance a log resolution of $\mathcal I(mu)$, then locally on $Y$ \[  K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m,\qquad b_ m	ext{ smooth and strictly positive},  \] where $s_ D$ is a local equation of $D$. The same conclusions hold if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$. Proof. We give the proof for the measure $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; Lebesgue measure is the case $\varrho =1$. By lemma 6.15.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space with an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$, evaluation is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Omega $, and ( 6.15.2 ) holds. We show that the map $z\mapsto (e_\ell (z))_\ell $ into $\ell ^2$ is given locally by a convergent power series with coefficients in $\ell ^2$. Fix a point $z_0$ and a polydisc $P$ of multiradius $ho $ about $z_0$ with $\overline P\subset \Omega $, and let $C$ be the evaluation bound on $\overline P$. For a finitely supported sequence $(c_\ell )$ with $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2\leq 1$, the function $F=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell $ has norm at most one, so $|F|\leq C$ on $P$, and the Cauchy estimates give $|\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !|\leq Cho ^{-\alpha }$. Since $\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !=\sum _\ell c_\ell A_{\alpha ,\ell }$ with $A_{\alpha ,\ell }=\partial ^\alpha e_\ell (z_0)/\alpha !$, taking the supremum over such sequences shows that the sequence $A_\alpha =(A_{\alpha ,\ell })_\ell $ has $\ell ^2$ norm $\| A_\alpha \| \leq Cho ^{-\alpha }$. Let $0<\lambda <1$, and let $P_\lambda $ be the concentric polydisc of multiradius $\lambda ho $. For $z\in P_\lambda $ we have $\sum _\alpha \| A_\alpha \| |(z-z_0)^\alpha |\leq C\sum _\alpha \lambda ^{|\alpha |}<\infty $, so the $\ell ^2$-valued series $\sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha $ converges absolutely, and its $\ell $th component is the Taylor series of $e_\ell $, which converges to $e_\ell (z)$. By ( 6.15.2 ), \[  K_ m(z)=\Bigl \| \sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha \Bigr \| ^2=\sum _{\alpha , eta }\langle A_\alpha ,A_ eta angle (z-z_0)^\alpha \overline{(z-z_0)^ eta },\qquad z\in P_\lambda ,  \] where $|\langle A_\alpha ,A_ eta angle |\leq C^2ho ^{-\alpha - eta }$. Hence this double power series, and each series obtained from it by differentiating term by term, converge uniformly on $P_{\lambda '}$ for every $\lambda '<\lambda $, since a derivative of order $k$ only introduces factors bounded by a polynomial of degree $k$ in $|\alpha |+| eta |$. Therefore $K_ m$ is real analytic, in particular smooth. Next choose members $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ of $H_ m$ generating $\mathcal I(mu)$ near a given point, by lemma 6.15.1 (2); by the remark following definition 6.14.5 , any other finite system of generators gives a comparable sum of squares. By the definition of $K_ m$, $|g_ i|^2\leq \| g_ i\| _ m^2K_ m$, so $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq  igl (\sum _ i\| g_ i\| _ m^2 igr )K_ m$. Conversely, lemma 6.15.1 (3) gives, on a fixed smaller neighborhood, a representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ with $|h_ i|\leq C'$ for every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. text: Lemma 6.15.1 . C2732E72E566 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, be a bounded pseudoconvex open set, let $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and let $\varrho $ be a measurable function on $\Omega $ with $c_\varrho \leq \varrho \leq C_\varrho $ for positive constants $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $. Put \[  \mathcal H=\Bigl \{ F\in \mathcal O(\Omega ):\| F\| ^2=\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV<\infty \Bigr \} ,\qquad \langle F,G\rangle =\int _\Omega F\bar G\, \mathrm e^{-\psi }\varrho \, \mathrm dV.  \] For every compact set $K\subset \Omega $ there is a constant $C_ K$ such that $|F(z)|\leq C_ K\| F\| $ for all $F\in \mathcal H$ and $z\in K$. The space $\mathcal H$ is a separable Hilbert space, and it has an orthonormal basis, that is, an orthonormal family $(e_\ell )$, finite or countable, whose linear span is dense. For every such family and every $F\in \mathcal H$, the partial sums of $\sum _\ell \langle F,e_\ell \rangle e_\ell $ converge to $F$ in norm and locally uniformly on $\Omega $, and $\sum _\ell |\langle F,e_\ell \rangle |^2=\| F\| ^2$. The germs of the elements of $\mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ at every point of $\Omega $, and near each point finitely many elements of $\mathcal H$ already generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$. Let $x\in \Omega $, and let $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s\in \mathcal H$ generate $\mathcal I(\psi )$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then there are a neighborhood $V$ of $x$ and a constant $C$ such that every $F\in \mathcal H$ can be written as $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ with $h_ i\in \mathcal O(V)$ and $\sup _ V|h_ i|\leq C\| F\| $. Proof. We regard $\Omega $ as a complex manifold, with the single chart given by the identity map. Then $\psi $ is a weight on $\Omega $ in the sense of section 6.8 , the set $\Omega $ satisfies the hypotheses of theorem 6.8.9 , and $\mathcal H$ is the space $\mathcal H_\psi (\Omega ,\varrho )$ of that theorem, with the same inner product. Hence (1) is contained in theorem 6.8.9 (1) and (2), and (2) follows from theorem 6.8.9 (3), because an initial segment of an enumerated orthonormal basis is a finite family of elements of $\mathcal H$. Finally, (3) is the first assertion of lemma 6.8.10 , applied to the weight $\psi $ on $\Omega $. $\square$

text: Lemma 6.15.3 . 09CBB2B6BA0F The function $K_ m$ is real analytic on $\Omega $. Near each point of $\Omega $ it is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, where $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ are finitely many generators of $\mathcal I(mu)$ near that point. If $\pi \colon Y\to \Omega $ is a holomorphic map from a complex manifold $Y$ such that $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)=\mathcal O_ Y(-D)$ for an effective divisor $D$ on $Y$, for instance a log resolution of $\mathcal I(mu)$, then locally on $Y$ \[  K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m,\qquad b_ m\text{ smooth and strictly positive},  \] where $s_ D$ is a local equation of $D$. The same conclusions hold if Lebesgue measure is replaced by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$ in the definition of $H_ m$. Proof. We give the proof for the measure $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; Lebesgue measure is the case $\varrho =1$. By lemma 6.15.1 , applied with $\psi =mu$, the space $H_ m$ is a Hilbert space with an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$, evaluation is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $\Omega $, and ( 6.15.2 ) holds. We show that the map $z\mapsto (e_\ell (z))_\ell $ into $\ell ^2$ is given locally by a convergent power series with coefficients in $\ell ^2$. Fix a point $z_0$ and a polydisc $P$ of multiradius $\rho $ about $z_0$ with $\overline P\subset \Omega $, and let $C$ be the evaluation bound on $\overline P$. For a finitely supported sequence $(c_\ell )$ with $\sum _\ell |c_\ell |^2\leq 1$, the function $F=\sum _\ell c_\ell e_\ell $ has norm at most one, so $|F|\leq C$ on $P$, and the Cauchy estimates give $|\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !|\leq C\rho ^{-\alpha }$. Since $\partial ^\alpha F(z_0)/\alpha !=\sum _\ell c_\ell A_{\alpha ,\ell }$ with $A_{\alpha ,\ell }=\partial ^\alpha e_\ell (z_0)/\alpha !$, taking the supremum over such sequences shows that the sequence $A_\alpha =(A_{\alpha ,\ell })_\ell $ has $\ell ^2$ norm $\| A_\alpha \| \leq C\rho ^{-\alpha }$. Let $0<\lambda <1$, and let $P_\lambda $ be the concentric polydisc of multiradius $\lambda \rho $. For $z\in P_\lambda $ we have $\sum _\alpha \| A_\alpha \| |(z-z_0)^\alpha |\leq C\sum _\alpha \lambda ^{|\alpha |}<\infty $, so the $\ell ^2$-valued series $\sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha $ converges absolutely, and its $\ell $th component is the Taylor series of $e_\ell $, which converges to $e_\ell (z)$. By ( 6.15.2 ), \[  K_ m(z)=\Bigl \| \sum _\alpha A_\alpha (z-z_0)^\alpha \Bigr \| ^2=\sum _{\alpha ,\beta }\langle A_\alpha ,A_\beta \rangle (z-z_0)^\alpha \overline{(z-z_0)^\beta },\qquad z\in P_\lambda ,  \] where $|\langle A_\alpha ,A_\beta \rangle |\leq C^2\rho ^{-\alpha -\beta }$. Hence this double power series, and each series obtained from it by differentiating term by term, converge uniformly on $P_{\lambda '}$ for every $\lambda '<\lambda $, since a derivative of order $k$ only introduces factors bounded by a polynomial of degree $k$ in $|\alpha |+|\beta |$. Therefore $K_ m$ is real analytic, in particular smooth. Next choose members $g_1,\ldots ,g_ s$ of $H_ m$ generating $\mathcal I(mu)$ near a given point, by lemma 6.15.1 (2); by the remark following definition 6.14.5 , any other finite system of generators gives a comparable sum of squares. By the definition of $K_ m$, $|g_ i|^2\leq \| g_ i\| _ m^2K_ m$, so $\sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq \bigl (\sum _ i\| g_ i\| _ m^2\bigr )K_ m$. Conversely, lemma 6.15.1 (3) gives, on a fixed smaller neighborhood, a representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ with $|h_ i|\leq C'$ for every $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|F|^2\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$, and hence $K_ m\leq sC'^2\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ there. These constants may depend on $m$, $u$ and $\varrho $. Let $\pi $ and $D$ be as in the statement, let $y\in Y$, let $V$ be a neighborhood of $\pi (y)$ on which the bounded representation of the previous paragraph holds, and let $s_ D$ be a local equation of $D$ on a neighborhood $W\subset \pi ^{-1}(V)$ of $y$. Since $\pi ^*\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $s_ D$ on $W$, we may write $g_ i\circ \pi =s_ Dk_ i$ and $s_ D=\sum _ il_ i\, (g_ i\circ \pi )$ with holomorphic $k_ i$ and $l_ i$, after shrinking $W$; since $s_ D$ does not vanish identically on any open set, $\sum _ il_ ik_ i=1$. For $F\in H_ m$, the representation $F=\sum _ ig_ ih_ i$ on $V$ gives $F\circ \pi =s_ D\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )k_ i$ on $W$, so \[  \frac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}=\sum _ i(h_ i\circ \pi )\, k_ i,\qquad \Bigl |\frac{F\circ \pi }{s_ D}\Bigr |\leq C'\| F\| _ m\sum _ i|k_ i|.  \] Hence evaluation of $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ is bounded on each compact subset of $W$, uniformly for $F$ in the unit ball of $H_ m$. The power-series argument above therefore applies, in local coordinates on $Y$, to the holomorphic functions $(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and shows that $b_ m=\sum _\ell |(e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D|^2$ is smooth; by ( 6.15.2 ), $K_ m\circ \pi =|s_ D|^2b_ m$. To see that $b_ m$ is strictly positive, let $F$ lie in the unit ball of $H_ m$, with coefficients $c_\ell =\langle F,e_\ell \rangle $ and partial sums $S_ N$. The estimate in the last display, applied to $F-S_ N$, shows that $(S_ N\circ \pi )/s_ D\to (F\circ \pi )/s_ D$ pointwise on $W$; hence $(F\circ \pi )/s_ D=\sum _\ell c_\ell (e_\ell \circ \pi )/s_ D$, and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality gives $|(F\circ \pi )/s_ D|^2\leq b_ m$. Taking $F=g_ i/\| g_ i\| _ m$ for the indices with $g_ i\neq 0$, we obtain $b_ m\geq |k_ i|^2/\| g_ i\| _ m^2$, and the functions $k_ i$ have no common zero. $\square$

The stalk $\mathcal I(mu)_ z$ is not zero: by the first paragraph, applied to the component of $\Omega $ containing $z$, it contains the germ of an element of $H_ m$ that does not vanish identically on that component, and this germ is not zero by the identity theorem. Since $u_ m=m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ near $z$, lemma 6.14.7 gives $
u (u_ m,z)=m^{-1}\operatorname {ord}_ z\mathcal I(mu)$, and ( 6.15.6 ) follows from lemma 6.9.1 . Finally, near each point $K_ m\leq C\sum _ i|g_ i|^2$ with $g_ i\in H_ m$, by lemma 6.15.3 , and each $|g_ i|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is integrable on $\Omega $. Hence $\exp (m(u_ m-u))=K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. Now replace Lebesgue measure by $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$, and let $K^\varrho _ m$ be the corresponding kernel. The space of holomorphic functions is the same, and the two norms satisfy $c_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2\leq \| F\| _{m,\varrho }^2\leq C_\varrho \| F\| _ m^2$. If $\| F\| _ m\leq 1$, then $F/C_\varrho ^{1/2}$ lies in the unit ball for $\varrho $, and if $\| F\| _{m,\varrho }\leq 1$, then $c_\varrho ^{1/2}F$ lies in the unit ball for Lebesgue measure; hence \[  C_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\leq K^\varrho _ m\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m.  \] The proof of plurisubharmonicity applies verbatim to $m^{-1}\log K^\varrho _ m$, with the unit ball taken for $\varrho $ and the continuity of $K^\varrho _ m$ given by lemma 6.15.3 . The lower and upper bounds follow from the last display, with the constants $C_\varrho C_1$ and $C_2/c_\varrho $. The convergence and the Lelong numbers then follow as before, since lemma 6.15.3 applies to $K^\varrho _ m$. Finally, $K^\varrho _ m\mathrm e^{-mu}\leq c_\varrho ^{-1}K_ m\mathrm e^{-mu}$ is locally integrable. $\square$

text: Lemma 6.15.7 . 365648DE5857 Suppose that the spaces $H_ m$ are defined with respect to $\varrho \, \mathrm dV$; for instance $\varrho =1$. There is a constant $C_\Omega >0$, depending only on $n$, on a bound $L$ for the diameter of $\Omega $ and on $c_\varrho $ and $C_\varrho $, and in particular independent of $m$ and $u$, such that \[  K_{2m}\leq C_\Omega K_ m^2\qquad \text{on }\Omega .  \] Proof. We write $\| \cdot \| _ m$ for the norm of $H_ m$. By the definition of $K_ m$, every $h\in H_ m$ satisfies $|h(\zeta )|^2\leq \| h\| _ m^2K_ m(\zeta )$ for all $\zeta \in \Omega $; if $\| h\| _ m=0$, then $h$ vanishes almost everywhere, hence identically. Let $F\in H_{2m}$. We first extend $F$ from the diagonal to $\Omega \times \Omega $. By corollary 6.3.5 , $\Omega \times \Omega $ is a bounded pseudoconvex open set in $\mathbb C^{2n}$, of diameter at most $\sqrt2L$, and the function $p(z,w)=mu(z)+mu(w)$ is plurisubharmonic on it (proposition 5.9.3 , proposition 5.9.5 ). The diagonal $\Lambda =\{ (z,w)\in \mathbb C^{2n}:z=w\} $ is a complex linear subspace of codimension $n$, and the map $z\mapsto (z,z)$ multiplies Euclidean lengths by $\sqrt2$, so Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda $ corresponds to $2^ n$ times Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb C^ n$. On $\Lambda \cap (\Omega \times \Omega )$, identified with $\Omega $, the weight $p$ restricts to $2mu$, so \[  \int _{\Lambda \cap (\Omega \times \Omega )}|F|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}=2^ n\int _\Omega |F|^2\mathrm e^{-2mu}\, \mathrm dV\leq 2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2.  \] The extension statement of corollary 6.5.8 , applied on $\Omega \times \Omega $ to the weight $p$ and the subspace $\Lambda $, gives $G\in \mathcal O(\Omega \times \Omega )$ with $G(z,z)=F(z)$ and $\int _{\Omega \times \Omega }|G|^2\mathrm e^{-p}\, \mathrm dV_{4n}\leq C^ n(\sqrt2L)^{2n}2^ nc_\varrho ^{-1}\| F\| _{2m}^2$, where $C$ is the constant of theorem 6.5.4 . Hence \[  \| G\| ^2=\int _{\Omega \times \Omega }|G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)-mu(w)}\varrho (z)\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(z)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2  \] with $C_\Omega =4^ nC^ nL^{2n}C_\varrho ^2/c_\varrho $. We now bound $G$ on the diagonal by $K_ m$. For $w\in \Omega $ put \[  N(w)=\int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(z)}\varrho (z)\, \mathrm dV(z)\in [0,\infty ].  \] By Tonelli's theorem, $N$ is measurable and $\int _\Omega N(w)\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)=\| G\| ^2<\infty $; since $\mathrm e^{-mu}\varrho >0$ almost everywhere, $N(w)<\infty $ for almost every $w$. For such $w$, the function $G(\cdot ,w)$ belongs to $H_ m$ with $\| G(\cdot ,w)\| _ m^2=N(w)$, so $|G(z,w)|^2\leq N(w)K_ m(z)$ for every $z$. Fix $z\in \Omega $. Integrating this inequality in $w$, we obtain \[  \int _\Omega |G(z,w)|^2\mathrm e^{-mu(w)}\varrho (w)\, \mathrm dV(w)\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2,  \] so $G(z,\cdot )\in H_ m$ with $\| G(z,\cdot )\| _ m^2\leq K_ m(z)\| G\| ^2$, and therefore $|G(z,w)|^2\leq K_ m(z)K_ m(w)\| G\| ^2$ for every $w$. Taking $w=z$, \[  |F(z)|^2=|G(z,z)|^2\leq K_ m(z)^2\| G\| ^2\leq C_\Omega \| F\| _{2m}^2K_ m(z)^2.  \] Taking the supremum over the unit ball of $H_{2m}$ proves the lemma. $\square$

title: Lemma 6.16.1

section: 6.16 Overlap interpolation and quantitative patching
text: Lemma 6.16.1 . 6A23B839899E Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $a\geq 0$, and let $v_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(B_ j,\theta )$ for $j=1,\ldots ,J$ satisfy $v_ j\leq v_ l+a$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ for all $j,l$. Then the function \[  v(x)=\max _{j:\, x\in \overline{U'_ j}}\bigl (v_ j(x)+a\chi _ j(x)\bigr )  \] is quasi-plurisubharmonic on $X$ and satisfies $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq -aC_\chi \omega $ and $v_ j\leq v\leq v_ j+2a$ on $U_ j$. Proof. Since the $U_ i$ cover $X$, the maximum is taken over a nonempty set at every point. Fix $x_0\in X$ and choose $i$ with $x_0\in U_ i$. Indices $j$ with $x_0\notin \overline{U'_ j}$ do not occur near $x_0$. If $x_0\in \partial U'_ j$, then $\chi _ j=0$ near $x_0$, because $\chi _ j$ has compact support in $U'_ j$; so near $x_0$ the $j$th term, where it is defined, equals $v_ j\leq v_ i+a=v_ i+a\chi _ i$, since $\chi _ i=1$ on the neighborhood $U_ i$ of $x_0$. Such a term never exceeds the $i$th term and can be omitted. Hence on a small neighborhood of $x_0$, $v$ is the maximum of $v_ j+a\chi _ j$ over the fixed set of indices $j$ with $x_0\in U'_ j$. Each of these functions satisfies $\theta +aC_\chi \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ j+a\chi _ j)\geq 0$. Adding a local potential of the closed form $\theta +aC_\chi \omega $ on a coordinate ball about $x_0$ (lemma 6.14.2 ), which makes these functions plurisubharmonic by lemma 6.14.4 (2), and applying proposition 5.9.5 , we obtain that $v$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic near $x_0$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\geq -aC_\chi \omega $. On $U_ j$ the $j$th term is $v_ j+a\geq v_ j$, and every term with index $l$ is at most $v_ l+a\leq v_ j+2a$. This proves the two bounds, also at points of the pole sets. $\square$

title: Lemma 6.16.2
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.16 Overlap interpolation and quantitative patching
text: Lemma 6.16.2 . 82376665E5F7 There is a constant $C_ B\geq 0$, depending only on the fixed geometry and in particular independent of $\theta $, $\varphi $ and $m$, such that \[  a_{j,m}\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}a_{l,m}\qquad \text{on }\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}  \] for all $j,l$. In particular $a_{j,m}$ and $a_{l,m}$ have the same zeros on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, and $|v_{j,m}-v_{l,m}|\leq C_ B/m$ there outside these common zeros. Proof. Fix $j,l$ with $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}\neq \varnothing $, and work in the coordinates of the ball $\mathcal B_{jl}$. By lemma 6.14.2 choose a smooth function $g$ on $\mathcal B_{jl}$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=\theta $. The functions $h_ j-g$ and $h_ l-g$ are pluriharmonic on the coordinate balls $B_ j^+$ and $B_ l^+$, so by the same lemma $h_ j-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ and $h_ l-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ l$ with $b_ j,b_ l$ holomorphic on these balls (the constants are absorbed into $b_ j,b_ l$). Put $u=\varphi +g$, a plurisubharmonic function on $\mathcal B_{jl}$. Since $|\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}|^2=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}$, multiplication by $\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}$ is an isometry from the weighted space defining $K_{j,m}$ onto the space of holomorphic functions on $B_ j$ with weight $mu$ and volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$. If $K^{mu}_{B_ j}$ denotes the Bergman kernel of the latter space, then $K^{mu}_{B_ j}=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}K_{j,m}$, and therefore \[  a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}K^{mu}_{B_ j},\qquad a_{l,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}K^{mu}_{B_ l}.  \] Hence it suffices to prove $K^{mu}_{B_ j}\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ with $C_0\geq 1$ depending only on the fixed geometry. Choose a smooth function $\rho \colon X\to [0,1]$ with compact support in $B_ j\cap B_ l$, equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact set $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ (proposition 5.2.6 ); this choice belongs to the fixed geometry. Let $r>0$ be the distance, in the coordinates of $\mathcal B_{jl}$, from $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$ to the support of $\bar\partial \rho $, and let $c>0$ and $C''$ be lower and upper bounds for the density of $\omega ^ n/n!$ with respect to Lebesgue measure on $B_ j\cup B_ l$ in these coordinates. The ball $B_ l$ is pseudoconvex also in the coordinates of $\mathcal B_{jl}$, since a biholomorphism transports a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion function (proposition 5.9.3 ). To compare the kernels at a point $x\in \overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, we correct $\rho f$, for $f$ holomorphic on $B_ j$, to a holomorphic function on $B_ l$ with the same value at $x$. Let $f$ be holomorphic on $B_ j$ with norm at most one in the weighted space, and extend $\rho f$ by zero to a smooth function on $B_ l$. We apply theorem 6.4.9 on $B_ l$ to the smooth $\bar\partial $-closed form $f\bar\partial \rho $, with the plurisubharmonic function $p=mu+n\log |z-x|^2$ and the smooth function $q=|z|^2$, whose complex Hessian matrix is the identity. On the support of $\bar\partial \rho $ we have $|z-x|^{-2n}\leq r^{-2n}$, so \[  \int _{B_ l}|f\bar\partial \rho |^2\mathrm e^{-p-q}\, \mathrm dV\leq r^{-2n}\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2\int _{B_ j}|f|^2\mathrm e^{-mu}\, \mathrm dV\leq \frac{\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2}{cr^{2n}}.  \] Hence there is a solution of $\bar\partial w=f\bar\partial \rho $ on $B_ l$ with \[  \int _{B_ l}|w|^2|z-x|^{-2n}\mathrm e^{-mu-|z|^2}\, \mathrm dV\leq C=\frac{\sup |\bar\partial \rho |^2}{cr^{2n}},  \] and $C$ depends only on the fixed geometry. The function $|z-x|^{2n}\mathrm e^{|z|^2}$ is bounded on the bounded set $B_ l$ by a constant of the same kind, and the density of $\omega ^ n/n!$ is at most $C''$. Hence the squared weighted norm of $w$, for the weight $mu$ and the volume form $\omega ^ n/n!$, is at most a constant $C'$ depending only on the fixed geometry. Near $x$ we have $\bar\partial w=f\bar\partial \rho =0$, because $\rho =1$ there; hence $\Delta w=0$ near $x$, and by theorem 3.1.11 $w$ is smooth, hence holomorphic, near $x$. Suppose that $w(x)\neq 0$. Then $|w|^2\geq |w(x)|^2/4$ on a ball $B(x,\delta )$ on which $u\leq M$ for some constant $M$, since $u$ is upper semicontinuous, and the last integral is at least \[  \frac{|w(x)|^2}4\, \mathrm e^{-mM-\sup _{B_ l}|z|^2}\int _{B(x,\delta )}|z-x|^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV=\infty ,  \] because $\int _{B(x,\delta )}|z-x|^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV=s_{2n-1}\int _0^\delta t^{-1}\, \mathrm dt$ in polar coordinates ( 3.1.2 ). Hence $w(x)=0$. The function $F=\rho f-w$ satisfies $\bar\partial F=0$ on $B_ l$, so it is holomorphic by theorem 3.1.11 , and $F(x)=f(x)$. Since $0\leq \rho \leq 1$ and $\rho $ vanishes outside $B_ j$, the weighted norm of $F$ on $B_ l$ is at most $1+C'^{1/2}=C_0$. By the definition of the kernel, $|f(x)|^2=|F(x)|^2\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}(x)$, and taking the supremum over $f$ gives $K^{mu}_{B_ j}(x)\leq C_0^2K^{mu}_{B_ l}(x)$. No bound on $u$, $\theta $ or $m$ enters these constants. Taking $C_ B$ to be the maximum of $2\log C_0$ over the finitely many pairs $(j,l)$, with the roles of $j$ and $l$ also exchanged, proves the lemma. $\square$

title: Theorem 6.16.3
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization

text: Theorem 6.16.3 . E9EBCA5A681D There is a constant $c>0$, depending only on $(X,\omega )$ through the fixed geometry, with the following property. Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and let $m\geq 1$ be an integer. Then there is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi _ m$ on $X$ such that \[  \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ m\geq -\frac cm\omega , \qquad \varphi _ m\geq \frac1m\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)\quad \text{locally},  \] where the $g_ i$ are local generators of $\mathcal I(m\varphi )$. The bounded term may depend on $m$, $\theta $, $\varphi $ and the point. Proof. By lemma 6.16.2 , the functions $v_{j,m}\in \mathrm{PSH}(B_ j,\theta )$ satisfy $v_{j,m}\leq v_{l,m}+C_ B/m$ on $\overline{U'_ j}\cap \overline{U'_ l}$, also at their common zeros. Hence lemma 6.16.1 with $a=C_ B/m$ gives a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi _ m$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ m\geq -(C_ BC_\chi /m)\omega $, so the first conclusion holds with $c=C_ BC_\chi $, increased if necessary to make it positive. On $U_ j$ the function $\varphi _ m$ dominates $v_{j,m}=m^{-1}\log K_{j,m}-h_ j$. Since $h_ j$ is smooth, $\mathcal I(m(\varphi +h_ j))=\mathcal I(m\varphi )$, and the comparison of lemma 6.15.3 gives $v_{j,m}\geq m^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ near each point of $U_ j$. This proves the second conclusion. $\square$

text:
The maximum in theorem 6.16.3 destroys smoothness, and that theorem does not compare the functions $\varphi _ m$ for different values of $m$. To obtain the regularity required of gentle singularities and, later, a decreasing sequence, we glue the local kernels instead by a sum with smooth cutoffs and control the curvature of its logarithm by a direct computation. We keep the notation of the previous section. Lemma 6.17.1 . EFA6E7FF99E6 Let $	heta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, let $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$, let $m\geq 1$ be an integer, and put \[  R_ m=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2a_{j,m},\qquad G_ m=m^{-1}\log R_ m,  \] each summand being extended by zero outside the support of $\chi _ j$. There is a constant $c'>0$, depending only on the fixed geometry, such that $	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}G_ m\geq -(c'/m)\omega $. Moreover $R_ m$ is smooth on $X$, and $G_ m$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(m\varphi ))$. Let $W$ be an open subset of a complex manifold, let $N\geq 1$, and let $w_1,\ldots ,w_ N$ and $\chi _1,\ldots ,\chi _ N$ be smooth real functions on $W$ such that $S=\sum _{j=1}^ N\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$ is positive on $W$. Put $\alpha _ j=\chi _ j\partial w_ j+2\partial \chi _ j$. Then, on $W$, 9F558292FE56 6.17.2  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log S={}&  rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi S^2} \sum _{j<l}\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l} (\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j) \wedge \overline{(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)}\ & + rac{\sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j}{S} +2 rac{\sum _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}  igl (\chi _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j- rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi } \partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j igr )}{S}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} and the first term on the right of ( 6.17.2 ) is a semipositive $(1,1)$-form. Proof. Step 1: proof of (2). Let $w_ j$, $\chi _ j$, $S$ and $\alpha _ j$ be as in (2), and put $f_ j=\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$, so that $S=\sum _ jf_ j$. Then $\partial f_ j=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}(\chi _ j\partial w_ j+2\partial \chi _ j)=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j$, so that $\partial S=\sum _ j\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j$. Since $\chi _ j$ and $w_ j$ are real, $ ar\partial f_ j=\overline{\partial f_ j}=\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j} ar\alpha _ j$ with $ ar\alpha _ j=\chi _ j ar\partial w_ j+2 ar\partial \chi _ j$, and \[   egin{aligned}  \partial  ar\partial f_ j& =\partial (\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j})\wedge  ar\alpha _ j+\chi _ j\mathrm e^{w_ j}\, \partial  ar\alpha _ j\ & =\mathrm e^{w_ j} igl ((\partial \chi _ j+\chi _ j\partial w_ j)\wedge (\chi _ j ar\partial w_ j+2 ar\partial \chi _ j)\ & \qquad +\chi _ j\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+\chi _ j^2\partial  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial  ar\partial \chi _ j igr )\ & =\mathrm e^{w_ j} igl (\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j+\chi _ j^2\partial  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial  ar\partial \chi _ j-2\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j igr ), \end{aligned}  \] where the last line follows by expanding $\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j=\chi _ j^2\partial w_ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+2\chi _ j\partial w_ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j+2\chi _ j\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial w_ j+4\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j$. Next, $\partial  ar\partial \log S=\partial  ar\partial S/S-\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S/S^2$, and since $\sum _ l\chi _ l^2\mathrm e^{w_ l}=S$, \[  \sum _ j rac{\mathrm e^{w_ j}\alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j}S- rac{\partial S\wedge  ar\partial S}{S^2} = rac1{S^2}\sum _{j,l}\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l} igl (\chi _ l^2\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ j-\chi _ j\chi _ l\, \alpha _ j\wedge  ar\alpha _ l igr ).  \] In the last sum the terms with $j=l$ vanish, and for $j<l$ the terms with indices $(j,l)$ and $(l,j)$ add up to $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)\wedge \overline{(\chi _ j\alpha _ l-\chi _ l\alpha _ j)}$. Multiplying by $\mathrm i/2\pi $ and using $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}= rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial  ar\partial $, we obtain ( 6.17.2 ). The first term on the right of ( 6.17.2 ) is semipositive, because the coefficients $\mathrm e^{w_ j+w_ l}/(2\pi S^2)$ are positive and, for a $(1,0)$-form $\gamma =\sum _ k\gamma _ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$, the coefficient matrix $(\gamma _ k ar\gamma _{k'})$ of $\mathrm i\gamma \wedge  ar\gamma $ is positive semidefinite. We now prove (1) in three steps. Step 2: a curvature estimate. By lemma 6.14.1 , applied on the compact manifold $X$ to the finitely many smooth forms below, there is a constant $A>0$, depending only on the fixed geometry, such that $\chi _ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ j- rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial \chi _ j\wedge  ar\partial \chi _ j\geq -A\omega $ for every $j$. Let $W\subset X$ be open, and for the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ let $w_ j$ be smooth real functions on $W$ such that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j\geq -m	heta \quad 	ext{on }W,\qquad \mathrm e^{w_ j}\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}\mathrm e^{w_ i}\quad 	ext{on }W\cap U_ i\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j  \] for all such $i,j$. We claim that $S=\sum _ j\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}$ is positive on $W$ and that \[  	heta + rac1m\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log S\geq - rac{2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}}m\omega \qquad 	ext{on }W.  \] Let $x\in W$ and choose $i$ with $x\in U_ i$. Then $\chi _ i(x)=1$, so $S(x)\geq \mathrm e^{w_ i(x)}>0$, and $\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S\leq \mathrm e^{C_ B}$ at $x$ for every $j$ with $\chi _ j(x)
eq 0$. Since $S>0$ on $W$, the identity ( 6.17.2 ) of (2) holds on $W$. If $\chi _ j(x)=0$, the $j$th summand of the last term in ( 6.17.2 ) vanishes at $x$, because the nonnegative function $\chi _ j$ attains its minimum at $x$, so that $\partial \chi _ j(x)=0$. Hence the last term is at least $-2JA\mathrm e^{C_ B}\omega $ at $x$. The coefficients $\chi _ j^2\mathrm e^{w_ j}/S$ are nonnegative with sum one, so the middle term is at least $-m	heta $, and the first term is semipositive. This proves the claim. Step 3: $G_ m$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and satisfies the curvature bound. Since the kernels $a_{j,m}$ may vanish, we apply Step 2 to smooth approximations of $\log a_{j,m}$ and pass to the limit. Fix $x_0\in X$ and a small coordinate ball $W$ about $x_0$ such that $W\subset U'_ j$ whenever $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$, and $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j=\varnothing $ otherwise; then the indices $j$ with $W\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j
eq \varnothing $ are those with $x_0\in \operatorname{Supp}\chi _ j$. Choose a smooth function $g$ on $W$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=	heta $, and for each such $j$ write $h_ j-g=\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$ with $b_ j$ holomorphic, by lemma 6.14.2 . Since $h_ j=g+\operatorname{Re}b_ j$ on $W$, we have $a_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mh_ j}K_{j,m}=\mathrm e^{-mg}k_ j$ on $W$, where, by ( 6.15.2 ) and since $|\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}|^2=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}$, $k_ j=\mathrm e^{-m\operatorname{Re}b_ j}K_{j,m}=\sum _\ell |\mathrm e^{-mb_ j/2}e_\ell |^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(e_\ell )$ of the space defining $K_{j,m}$. title: Lemma 6.17.4
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.17 Smooth cutoff sums and decreasing approximation
text: Lemma 6.17.4 . 7EFB7FFA3AB8 Let $u,v$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic near a point $x$ of a complex manifold, and let $m>0$ be such that $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$ is integrable near $x$. If $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ and $m\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then \[  \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x.  \] Proof. After shrinking the neighborhood we may subtract a constant from $v$ and assume $v\leq 0$; this changes neither the ideals nor the integrability of $\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Put $p=\lambda '/\lambda >1$, and note that $m\geq \lambda p/(p-1)>\lambda $. Let $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda 'v)_ x$, defined on a small neighborhood on which $|f|^2\leq C$ for a constant $C$. All the following inequalities are taken outside the pole sets of $u$ and $v$, which have measure zero. Where $u\geq pv$, we have $\lambda u\geq \lambda 'v$ and hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq |f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda 'v}$. Where $u<pv$, since $m-\lambda >0$, $v\leq 0$ and $(m-\lambda )p-m=m(p-1)-\lambda p\geq 0$, \[  (m-\lambda )u-mv\leq ((m-\lambda )p-m)v\leq 0,  \] that is, $-\lambda u\leq m(v-u)$; hence $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-\lambda u}\leq C\mathrm e^{m(v-u)}$. Both bounds are integrable near $x$, so $f\in \mathcal I(\lambda u)_ x$. $\square$

text: Definition 6.17.5 . 165F88FAE668 Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ and $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. A quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ is a sequence $(\Phi _ j)_{j\geq 1}$ of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions with analytic singularities, decreasing pointwise to $\varphi $, such that $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -\varepsilon _ j\omega $ for some numbers $\varepsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, and such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }j.  \] Definition 6.17.5 . 165F88FAE668 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold and $\theta $ be a closed real smooth $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Consider $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$. A sequence $(\varphi _ j)_{j\in \mathbb {Z}_{>0}}$ in $\mathrm{QPSH}(X)$ is quasi-equisingular approximation of $\varphi $ if 46C84A9DAE79 $\varphi _ j$ has analytic singularities for each $j$; B059E004A0A9 $\varphi _ j$ is decreasing with limit $\varphi $; E413383CB676 there is a decreasing sequence $\epsilon _ j\geq 0$ with limit $0$ and a Kähler form $\omega $ on $X$ such that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta +\epsilon _ j\omega )$; 82DBC1A3025C for each $\lambda '>\lambda >0$, there is $j>0$ such that EF5655B5F536 5.18.9 \begin{equation}  \mathcal{I}(\lambda ' \varphi _ j)\subseteq \mathcal{I}(\lambda \varphi ). \end{equation} We also say $(\theta _{\varphi _ j})_ j$ is a quasi-equisingular approximation of $\theta _{\varphi }$.

title: Theorem 6.17.6
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.17 Smooth cutoff sums and decreasing approximation
text: Theorem 6.17.6 . 080EF8C715CF Let $\theta $ be a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$. Every $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ admits a quasi-equisingular approximation $(\Phi _ j)$ in which each $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$, and which can be chosen with $\varepsilon _ j=c'2^{-j}$, where $c'$ is the constant of lemma 6.17.1 (1). Moreover $\Phi _ j\to \varphi $ in $L^1(X)$, and the Lelong numbers of $\Phi _ j$ satisfy the bounds of lemma 6.17.3 with $m=2^ j$. Proof. Put $\Phi _ j=G_{2^ j}+2D/2^ j$, with $D$ as in lemma 6.17.3 . The doubling inequality gives \[  \Phi _{j+1}=G_{2\cdot 2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}\leq G_{2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}+\frac D{2^ j}=\Phi _ j,  \] so the sequence is decreasing, and by lemma 6.17.3 its pointwise and $L^1$ limit is $\varphi $. Adding a constant changes neither the curvature, nor the analytic type, nor the Lelong numbers. Moreover $\exp (2^ j\Phi _ j)=\mathrm e^{2D}R_{2^ j}$ is smooth, and the remainder on a log resolution changes only by a constant. Hence $\Phi _ j$ has gentle analytic singularities of type $(2^{-j},\mathcal I(2^ j\varphi ))$ by lemma 6.17.1 (1), and $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ j\geq -c'2^{-j}\omega $. It remains to prove the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Let $0<\lambda <\lambda '$. The function $\exp (2^ j(\Phi _ j-\varphi ))=\mathrm e^{2D}\mathrm e^{2^ j(G_{2^ j}-\varphi )}$ is integrable on $X$ by lemma 6.17.3 . If $j$ is so large that $2^ j\geq \lambda \lambda '/(\lambda '-\lambda )$, then lemma 6.17.4 , with $u=\varphi $, $v=\Phi _ j$ and $m=2^ j$, gives $\mathcal I(\lambda '\Phi _ j)_ x\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi )_ x$ at every point $x\in X$. Since this threshold for $j$ depends only on $\lambda $ and $\lambda '$, the inclusion holds as an inclusion of sheaves on $X$ for all such $j$. $\square$

title: 6.18 Comparison of analytic singularities
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.18 Comparison of analytic singularities
text: For functions $u,v\colon X\to [-\infty ,\infty )$ we write $u\preceq v$, and say that $u$ is more singular than $v$, if $u\leq v+C$ on $X$ for some constant $C$. Since $X$ is compact, it suffices that every point have a neighborhood on which such an inequality holds. We now show that two quasi-equisingular approximations of the same function are comparable for $\preceq $, up to an arbitrarily small loss in the coefficient. The key is a growth estimate for the members of the multiplier ideals of a function with analytic singularities. Lemma 6.18.1 . BA49EE8EFFB8 Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function with analytic singularities on a compact complex manifold $X$, and let $0<\eta <1$. There is $t_0>0$ such that for every real $t\geq t_0$ and every germ $f\in \mathcal I(tv)_ x$, $x\in X$, \[  \log |f|^2\leq t(1-\eta )v+O(1)  \] near $x$, where the bounded term may depend on $f$. Moreover, for every quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$ and every $t>0$, local generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(tu)$ satisfy \[  u\leq t^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1).  \] Proof. For the first assertion we pull $v$ back to log resolutions of its local presentations, where theorem 6.12.8 bounds the vanishing orders of $f$ along the components of the divisor from below. Cover $X$ by finitely many open sets $V_\kappa ^+$ on which $v$ has a presentation ( 6.14.6 ), and choose open sets $V_\kappa \Subset V_\kappa ^+$ that still cover $X$. By theorem 9.6.7 , the ideal generated by the presentation on $V_\kappa ^+$ has a log resolution $\pi _\kappa \colon Y_\kappa \to V_\kappa ^+$, a sequence of blowups that is finite over $V_\kappa $; it is proper and surjective, so $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$ and the fibers of $\pi _\kappa $ are compact. On $Y_\kappa $ we have locally $v\circ \pi _\kappa =\sum _ Ea_ E\log |s_ E|^2+O(1)$, where $\pi _\kappa ^*(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r)=\mathcal O(-\sum _ Ed_ EE)$, $E$ runs over the components of this divisor, $s_ E$ is a local equation of $E$, and $a_ E=cd_ E>0$. Let $A_ E$ be the log discrepancy of $E$ (definition 6.12.3 ). Only finitely many components $E$ meet the compact set $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$, so altogether there are finitely many pairs $(a_ E,A_ E)$ with $E$ meeting one of these sets. Choose $t_0>0$ with $t_0\eta a_ E\geq A_ E$ for all of them. Now let $x\in V_\kappa $, let $t\geq t_0$, and let $f\in \mathcal I(tv)_ x$ be defined on an open neighborhood $V'\subset V_\kappa $ of $x$. Near $x$ the function $tv$ differs by a smooth function from a plurisubharmonic function with the same multiplier ideal and of the form required in theorem 6.12.8 , with coefficient $tc$. We apply that theorem over $V'$, shrunk if necessary, to the log resolution obtained by restricting $\pi _\kappa $. Each component $E'$ of the restricted divisor is a connected component of $E\cap \pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$ for a component $E$ as above, and it has the same coefficient $d_ E$ and the same log discrepancy $A_ E$, as we show below. Since $tc\, d_ E=ta_ E$, the theorem gives \[  \operatorname {ord}_{E'}f>ta_ E-A_ E\geq t(1-\eta )a_ E  \] for every component $E'$ of the restricted divisor that meets $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$; the second inequality holds because $t\geq t_0$ and $E$ meets $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(\overline{V_\kappa })$. The coefficient and the log discrepancy of $E'$ are those of $E$ because the vanishing orders along $E$ of a local generator of $\pi _\kappa ^*(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r)$ and of a local Jacobian determinant of $\pi _\kappa $ do not depend on the point of $E$ at which they are computed. Indeed, two local generators of this invertible ideal, like two local Jacobian determinants, differ by a unit, which has order zero along $E$; since orders add under products, they have the same order along $E$ at every point of $E$ where both are defined (lemma 6.12.1 (2),(4)). Moreover, the order along $E$ of a holomorphic function is locally constant on $E_{\mathrm{reg}}$, by the last assertion of lemma 6.12.1 (2), and $E_{\mathrm{reg}}$ is connected (corollary 9.3.16 ); here $E_{\mathrm{reg}}=E$, since the components of a simple normal crossings divisor are smooth. If $f=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $f\neq 0$. Shrinking $V'$, we may assume that $V'$ is connected; then $f$ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $V'$. Hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$, because $\pi _\kappa $ is a biholomorphism off the nowhere dense set $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r))$; in particular, the orders of $f$ along the components of the restricted divisor are finite. Let $p\in \pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and choose coordinates $w$ on a neighborhood of $p$ in $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$ in which the components of the divisor through $p$ are $\{ w_ k=0\} $, $k=1,\ldots ,\ell $, with coefficients $a_ k=a_ E$ for the corresponding components $E$. Then $v\circ \pi _\kappa =\sum _ ka_ k\log |w_ k|^2+O(1)$ near $p$. For each $k$, let $E'_ k$ be the component of the restricted divisor that contains $\{ w_ k=0\} $ near $p$, and put $o_ k=\operatorname {ord}_{E'_ k}f$, an integer with $o_ k>t(1-\eta )a_ k$ by the inequality above. Since $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is holomorphic on a neighborhood of $E'_ k$, its order along $E'_ k$ is the same at all points of the connected submanifold $E'_ k$, by lemma 6.12.1 (3); hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is divisible by $w_ k^{o_ k}$ near $p$, by lemma 6.12.1 (1),(2). By the last assertion of lemma 6.12.2 , divisibility by each $w_ k^{o_ k}$ separately implies divisibility by their product: $f\circ \pi _\kappa =\prod _ kw_ k^{o_ k}\cdot h$ with $h$ holomorphic near $p$, hence bounded on a smaller neighborhood of $p$. Since $|w_ k|\leq 1$ there, we obtain $|f\circ \pi _\kappa |^2\leq C\prod _ k|w_ k|^{2t(1-\eta )a_ k}\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v\circ \pi _\kappa )$. Finitely many such neighborhoods cover the compact fiber $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and since $\pi _\kappa $ is proper, their union contains the inverse image of a neighborhood of $x$. As $\pi _\kappa $ is surjective, the inequality $|f|^2\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v)$ holds near $x$. For the second assertion, fix a point and write $u=u_0-\sigma $ near it, with $u_0$ plurisubharmonic and $\sigma $ smooth. Then $\mathcal I(tu)=\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point. On a bounded polydisc $\Omega $ about the point on which $u_0$ is bounded above, theorem 6.8.9 (3) provides finitely many elements of $\mathcal H_{tu_0}(\Omega )$ that generate $\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point, and ( 6.8.11 ) of lemma 6.8.10 , applied with $m=t$ to the weight $u_0$, gives $u_0\leq t^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ for these generators. Since $\sigma $ is bounded near the point, and any two finite systems of local generators give comparable sums of squares (the remark following definition 6.14.5 ), the assertion follows. $\square$ Proposition 6.18.2 . 649F62FDFBAD Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, let $\varphi $ and $\Phi $ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ with $\varphi \leq \Phi $, where $\Phi $ has analytic singularities, and let $(\Psi _ k)_{k\geq 1}$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Psi _ k)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] Then for each $0<\varepsilon <1$, \[  \Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] In particular, if $(X,\omega )$ is a compact Kähler manifold, $\theta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $(\Phi _ j)$ and $(\Psi _ k)$ are quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $, then for each $j$ and each $0<\varepsilon <1$ we have $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi _ j$ for every sufficiently large $k$. Proof. Choose $0<\eta <\varepsilon $ and $\delta >0$ so small that $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $. Fix $t\geq t_0$, where $t_0$ is given by lemma 6.18.1 for $v=\Phi $ and $\eta $. By the hypothesis on $(\Psi _ k)$, applied with $\lambda =t$ and $\lambda '=t(1+\delta )$, and since $\varphi \leq \Phi $, \[  \mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k) \subseteq \mathcal I(t\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal I(t\Phi )  \] for every sufficiently large $k$. Fix such a $k$ and choose local generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k)$ near a point of $X$. They belong to $\mathcal I(t\Phi )$, so the first part of lemma 6.18.1 gives $\log |g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$ near the point, and hence $\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$. Its second part, applied to $u=\Psi _ k$ and $t(1+\delta )$, then gives \[  \Psi _ k\leq \frac1{t(1+\delta )}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1) \leq \frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }\Phi +O(1).  \] The upper semicontinuous function $\Phi $ is bounded above on the compact space $X$, say by $M$. Since $\Phi -M\leq 0$ and $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $, we have $\frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }(\Phi -M)\leq (1-\varepsilon )(\Phi -M)$, and therefore $\Psi _ k\leq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi +O(1)$ near every point. By compactness $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi $; the constant may depend on $k$. For the last assertion, recall from definition 6.17.5 that each $\Phi _ j$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic with analytic singularities and that $\varphi \leq \Phi _ j$, since the sequence decreases to $\varphi $; and $(\Psi _ k)$ satisfies the hypothesis on the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Hence the first part applies with $\Phi =\Phi _ j$. $\square$ Example 6.18.3 . E35B96BEFDE2 Let $u=c\log |z|^2$ on a disc about $0\in \mathbb C$, with $c>0$. A germ $z^ kh$ with $h(0)\neq 0$ lies in $\mathcal I(mu)_0$ if and only if $|z|^{2k-2mc}$ is integrable near $0$, that is, $k>mc-1$; hence $\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $z^{\lfloor mc\rfloor }$ (example 6.11.8 ). A potential of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(mu))$, such as the Bergman potential $u_ m$ of theorem 6.15.4 , is therefore $(\lfloor mc\rfloor /m)\log |z|^2+O(1)$ near $0$. Its coefficient $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m$ need not equal $c$ for any $m$, and then such an approximation does not reproduce the multiplier ideals of $u$ at a fixed scale. For instance, let $c$ be irrational, so that $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m<c$ for every $m$, and take the scale $1/c$. Since $u_ m/c$ differs by a bounded function from $c_ m\log |z|^2$ with $c_ m=\lfloor mc\rfloor /(mc)<1$, the same computation gives $\mathcal I(u_ m/c)_0=\mathcal O_0$ for every $m$, whereas $\mathcal I(u/c)_0=\mathcal I(\log |z|^2)_0$ is generated by $z$. This is why definition 6.17.5 compares two different scales $\lambda '>\lambda $ instead of requiring equality of multiplier ideals.

If $f=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $f\neq 0$. Shrinking $V'$, we may assume that $V'$ is connected; then $f$ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $V'$. Hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ does not vanish identically on any nonempty open subset of $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$, because $\pi _\kappa $ is a biholomorphism off the nowhere dense set $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V(g_1,\ldots ,g_ r))$; in particular, the orders of $f$ along the components of the restricted divisor are finite. Let $p\in \pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and choose coordinates $w$ on a neighborhood of $p$ in $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(V')$ in which the components of the divisor through $p$ are $\{ w_ k=0\} $, $k=1,\ldots ,\ell $, with coefficients $a_ k=a_ E$ for the corresponding components $E$. Then $v\circ \pi _\kappa =\sum _ ka_ k\log |w_ k|^2+O(1)$ near $p$. For each $k$, let $E'_ k$ be the component of the restricted divisor that contains $\{ w_ k=0\} $ near $p$, and put $o_ k=\operatorname {ord}_{E'_ k}f$, an integer with $o_ k>t(1-\eta )a_ k$ by the inequality above. Since $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is holomorphic on a neighborhood of $E'_ k$, its order along $E'_ k$ is the same at all points of the connected submanifold $E'_ k$, by lemma 6.12.1 (3); hence $f\circ \pi _\kappa $ is divisible by $w_ k^{o_ k}$ near $p$, by lemma 6.12.1 (1),(2). By the last assertion of lemma 6.12.2 , divisibility by each $w_ k^{o_ k}$ separately implies divisibility by their product: $f\circ \pi _\kappa =\prod _ kw_ k^{o_ k}\cdot h$ with $h$ holomorphic near $p$, hence bounded on a smaller neighborhood of $p$. Since $|w_ k|\leq 1$ there, we obtain $|f\circ \pi _\kappa |^2\leq C\prod _ k|w_ k|^{2t(1-\eta )a_ k}\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v\circ \pi _\kappa )$. Finitely many such neighborhoods cover the compact fiber $\pi _\kappa ^{-1}(x)$, and since $\pi _\kappa $ is proper, their union contains the inverse image of a neighborhood of $x$. As $\pi _\kappa $ is surjective, the inequality $|f|^2\leq C'\exp (t(1-\eta )v)$ holds near $x$. For the second assertion, fix a point and write $u=u_0-\sigma $ near it, with $u_0$ plurisubharmonic and $\sigma $ smooth. Then $\mathcal I(tu)=\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point. On a bounded polydisc $\Omega $ about the point on which $u_0$ is bounded above, theorem 6.8.9 (3) provides finitely many elements of $\mathcal H_{tu_0}(\Omega )$ that generate $\mathcal I(tu_0)$ near the point, and ( 6.8.11 ) of lemma 6.8.10 , applied with $m=t$ to the weight $u_0$, gives $u_0\leq t^{-1}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1)$ for these generators. Since $\sigma $ is bounded near the point, and any two finite systems of local generators give comparable sums of squares (the remark following definition 6.14.5 ), the assertion follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 6.18.2
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.18 Comparison of analytic singularities
text: Proposition 6.18.2 . 649F62FDFBAD Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, let $\varphi $ and $\Phi $ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ with $\varphi \leq \Phi $, where $\Phi $ has analytic singularities, and let $(\Psi _ k)_{k\geq 1}$ be quasi-plurisubharmonic functions on $X$ such that for all $0<\lambda <\lambda '$ \[  \mathcal I(\lambda '\Psi _ k)\subseteq \mathcal I(\lambda \varphi ) \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] Then for each $0<\varepsilon <1$, \[  \Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi \quad \text{for every sufficiently large }k.  \] In particular, if $(X,\omega )$ is a compact Kähler manifold, $\theta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form on $X$, $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $(\Phi _ j)$ and $(\Psi _ k)$ are quasi-equisingular approximations of $\varphi $, then for each $j$ and each $0<\varepsilon <1$ we have $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi _ j$ for every sufficiently large $k$. Proof. Choose $0<\eta <\varepsilon $ and $\delta >0$ so small that $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $. Fix $t\geq t_0$, where $t_0$ is given by lemma 6.18.1 for $v=\Phi $ and $\eta $. By the hypothesis on $(\Psi _ k)$, applied with $\lambda =t$ and $\lambda '=t(1+\delta )$, and since $\varphi \leq \Phi $, \[  \mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k) \subseteq \mathcal I(t\varphi )\subseteq \mathcal I(t\Phi )  \] for every sufficiently large $k$. Fix such a $k$ and choose local generators $g_ i$ of $\mathcal I(t(1+\delta )\Psi _ k)$ near a point of $X$. They belong to $\mathcal I(t\Phi )$, so the first part of lemma 6.18.1 gives $\log |g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$ near the point, and hence $\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2\leq t(1-\eta )\Phi +O(1)$. Its second part, applied to $u=\Psi _ k$ and $t(1+\delta )$, then gives \[  \Psi _ k\leq \frac1{t(1+\delta )}\log \sum _ i|g_ i|^2+O(1) \leq \frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }\Phi +O(1).  \] The upper semicontinuous function $\Phi $ is bounded above on the compact space $X$, say by $M$. Since $\Phi -M\leq 0$ and $(1-\eta )/(1+\delta )\geq 1-\varepsilon $, we have $\frac{1-\eta }{1+\delta }(\Phi -M)\leq (1-\varepsilon )(\Phi -M)$, and therefore $\Psi _ k\leq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi +O(1)$ near every point. By compactness $\Psi _ k\preceq (1-\varepsilon )\Phi $; the constant may depend on $k$. For the last assertion, recall from definition 6.17.5 that each $\Phi _ j$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic with analytic singularities and that $\varphi \leq \Phi _ j$, since the sequence decreases to $\varphi $; and $(\Psi _ k)$ satisfies the hypothesis on the inclusions of multiplier ideals. Hence the first part applies with $\Phi =\Phi _ j$. $\square$

title: Example 6.18.3
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.18 Comparison of analytic singularities
text: Example 6.18.3 . E35B96BEFDE2 Let $u=c\log |z|^2$ on a disc about $0\in \mathbb C$, with $c>0$. A germ $z^ kh$ with $h(0)\neq 0$ lies in $\mathcal I(mu)_0$ if and only if $|z|^{2k-2mc}$ is integrable near $0$, that is, $k>mc-1$; hence $\mathcal I(mu)$ is generated by $z^{\lfloor mc\rfloor }$ (example 6.11.8 ). A potential of type $(m^{-1},\mathcal I(mu))$, such as the Bergman potential $u_ m$ of theorem 6.15.4 , is therefore $(\lfloor mc\rfloor /m)\log |z|^2+O(1)$ near $0$. Its coefficient $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m$ need not equal $c$ for any $m$, and then such an approximation does not reproduce the multiplier ideals of $u$ at a fixed scale. For instance, let $c$ be irrational, so that $\lfloor mc\rfloor /m<c$ for every $m$, and take the scale $1/c$. Since $u_ m/c$ differs by a bounded function from $c_ m\log |z|^2$ with $c_ m=\lfloor mc\rfloor /(mc)<1$, the same computation gives $\mathcal I(u_ m/c)_0=\mathcal O_0$ for every $m$, whereas $\mathcal I(u/c)_0=\mathcal I(\log |z|^2)_0$ is generated by $z$. This is why definition 6.17.5 compares two different scales $\lambda '>\lambda $ instead of requiring equality of multiplier ideals.

title: 6.19 Bounded growth ideals

section: 6.19 Bounded growth ideals

A germ $f$ belongs to the multiplier ideal $\mathcal I(v)$ when $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-v}$ is integrable, a condition that allows $f$ to vanish to a slightly lower order than the growth of $\mathrm e^ v$ suggests. The stricter condition $|f|^2\leq C\mathrm e^ v$ defines a smaller ideal. For a weight $v$ with analytic singularities we prove that this ideal sheaf is coherent (theorem 6.19.2 ) and that, on a compact manifold, the ideal attached to $kv$ contains $\mathcal I(k(1+\varepsilon )v)$ for all large $k$ (corollary 6.19.3 ). In the proof of coherence, the condition $|f|\leq C|g|^{p/q}$ for a tuple $g$ of holomorphic functions becomes a holomorphic one: on the normalization of a root cover of a cone over the blowup of the ideal $(g)$, it is the holomorphy of a function homogeneous of weight $p$. Definition 6.19.1 . 574EEB86E59F Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold $X$. The bounded growth ideal $\mathcal I_\infty (v)$ is the sheaf of holomorphic germs $f$ satisfying \[  \log |f|^2\leq v+O(1), \quad 	ext{equivalently}\quad |f|^2\leq C\exp (v),  \] on a neighborhood of their base point, for some finite constant $C$. The zero germ belongs to $\mathcal I_\infty (v)$, and $\mathcal I_\infty (v)$ does not change if $v$ is changed by a bounded function. It is a sheaf of ideals, because $|f+g|^2\leq 2|f|^2+2|g|^2$ and holomorphic coefficients are locally bounded. It is contained in $\mathcal I(v)$, since $|f|^2\mathrm e^{-v}$ is locally bounded for $f\in \mathcal I_\infty (v)$. Theorem 6.19.2 . 993CE3FB0997 Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function with analytic singularities on a complex manifold $X$. Then $\mathcal I_\infty (v)$ is a coherent ideal sheaf. title: Definition 6.19.1
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
section: 6.19 Bounded growth ideals
text: Definition 6.19.1 . 574EEB86E59F Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold $X$. The bounded growth ideal $\mathcal I_\infty (v)$ is the sheaf of holomorphic germs $f$ satisfying \[  \log |f|^2\leq v+O(1), \quad \text{equivalently}\quad |f|^2\leq C\exp (v),  \] on a neighborhood of their base point, for some finite constant $C$.

text: Corollary 6.19.3 . BA0E41A3C821 Let $v$ be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function with analytic singularities on a compact complex manifold $X$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is $k_0>0$ such that for every real $k\geq k_0$ \[  \mathcal I(k(1+\varepsilon )v)\subseteq \mathcal I_\infty (kv).  \] Proof. Apply lemma 6.18.1 with $\eta =\varepsilon /(1+\varepsilon )$ and $t=k(1+\varepsilon )$, so that $t(1-\eta )=k$. The lemma provides one threshold $t_0$ for all germs on $X$; put $k_0=t_0/(1+\varepsilon )$. For $k\geq k_0$, every germ $f\in \mathcal I(k(1+\varepsilon )v)$ satisfies $\log |f|^2\leq kv+O(1)$ near its base point, that is, $f\in \mathcal I_\infty (kv)$. In dimension zero all these ideals are the unit ideal. $\square$

title: 10.1 Global potentials and positive cohomology classes

section: 10.1 Global potentials and positive cohomology classes
text: Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold, and let $T$ be a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $X$. By theorem 5.4.3 , every point of $X$ has a coordinate neighborhood on which $T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ with $u$ plurisubharmonic. On the overlap of two such neighborhoods the two local potentials differ by a pluriharmonic function, and in general no choice of the local potentials makes them agree. For instance, let $X$ have positive dimension and let $T=\omega $ be a Kähler form. A global potential $u$ would be plurisubharmonic on $X$, so it would attain its maximum, being upper semicontinuous on the compact space $X$. The set where it does so is closed, and it is also open by the maximum principle (proposition 3.4.7 ), applied on coordinate balls, where $u$ is subharmonic (theorem 5.9.1 ). Thus $u$ would be constant and $\omega =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=0$. The obstruction is the cohomology class of $T$: by the $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-lemma (theorem 10.2.15 ), if $\theta $ is a smooth closed form in the class of $T$, then $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi $ on $X$, unique up to an additive constant. We prove this by solving a Laplace equation for the trace of $T$, after developing the elliptic theory that this requires from the beginning; the same argument shows that the real $(1,1)$-cohomology of $X$ is finite dimensional. Closed positive currents in the class of $\theta $ therefore correspond, up to additive constants, to the functions in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ (definition 6.14.3 ), and the subsequent constructions works with such potentials. Once the additive constant is fixed by normalizing the supremum, the local compactness and integrability theorems for plurisubharmonic functions become uniform statements on $X$, and the upper envelope $V_\theta $ of the nonpositive potentials has minimal singularities. With these tools and the Demailly approximation of section 6.13 we study the positivity of a class (pseudo-effective, nef, big or Kähler) and the places where it fails. Siu's decomposition (theorem 10.4.8 ) splits off the divisorial part of a current. The minimal multiplicities of a class and its non-nef locus locate the points at which the positive currents in the class are forced to be singular, and the non-Kähler locus does the same for Kähler currents; we also compare these notions on $X$ and on a modification of $X$. A mixed version of the scalar equation gives the mixed Hodge index theorem (theorem 10.4.3 ) and inequalities between intersection numbers. The second half of the chapter concerns a holomorphic line bundle $L$ on $X$. If $h_0$ is a smooth metric on $L$ with curvature form $c_1(L,h_0)$, a singular metric $h_0\mathrm e^{-\varphi }$ with $\varphi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,c_1(L,h_0))$ is the global form of a plurisubharmonic weight; the metrics defined by finitely many holomorphic sections of powers of $L$ are examples with analytic singularities. We prove the $L^2$ estimate for $\bar\partial $ on line bundles over Kähler manifolds and combine it with the local extension theorems of section 6.1 to construct global sections with a prescribed value at a point (theorem 10.7.9 ) or a prescribed restriction to a compact submanifold (theorem 10.8.18 ), with constants that depend only on the geometry. We also describe the weighted spaces of global sections through their Bergman kernels. A related gluing construction extends strictly positive potentials from a submanifold (theorem 10.8.26 ). In the last section we leave the Kähler setting and prove Josefson's theorem on a compact complex manifold: every pluripolar set lies in the pole set of a single quasi-plurisubharmonic function (theorem 10.9.19 ). Historical remarks and references for this chapter are collected in subsection 25.1.14 .
