Lemma 10.9.4 . 04C8B0EA1481 Let $u,v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ be bounded, put $E=\{ u<v\} $, and let $T$ be a product of $n-1$ factors, each equal to $\omega $, $\omega _ u$ or $\omega _ v$. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ is a real measure on $X$, that is, a real current of order zero and degree $2n$, and F6D79B7B476D 10.9.5  egin{equation}  \int _ E(\omega _ v-\omega _ u)\wedge T \leq \int _ E(v-u)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T, \end{equation} where $(\omega _ v-\omega _ u)\wedge T=\omega _ v\wedge T-\omega _ u\wedge T$. Moreover, there is a constant $C$ depending only on $(X,\omega )$ such that the total variation $|\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T|$ of this measure satisfies FFED91B6BA32 10.9.6  egin{equation}  |\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T|\leq C\Bigl (\sum _ iT_{\hat\imath }\wedge \omega ^2+\sum _{i<i'}T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}\wedge \omega ^3\Bigr ). \end{equation} Here $T_{\hat\imath }$ denotes the product of the factors of $T$ other than the $i$th one, $T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}$ the product of those other than the $i$th and the $i'$th, and empty sums are zero. Proof. After computing $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ (Step 1), we prove a version of ( 10.9.5 ) in which $\mathbf1_ E$ is smoothed by a convex cutoff, integrating by parts against regularizations of $u$ and $v$ (Step 2). The products $T$, $T_{\hat\imath }$ and $T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}$ are positive currents: for products with at least one factor this is lemma 10.9.3 (2), and the empty product is the constant $1$. (If $n=1$, then $T=1$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0$, and both sums in ( 10.9.6 ) are empty; the sum over pairs is empty also if $n=2$.) Step 1. The measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$. Work on an open subset of a chart with $q$ and $\sigma $ as in ( 10.9.2 ). Each factor of $T$ has the form $\Theta _ i+\sigma $, where $\Theta _ i$ is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+q)$ or $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+q)$; thus $T=\sum _ J\Theta _ J\wedge \sigma ^{n-1-|J|}$, where $\Theta _ J$ is the Bedford–Taylor product of the $\Theta _ i$ with $i\in J$. The currents $\Theta _ J$ are closed of pure bidegree, so $\partial \Theta _ J= ar\partial \Theta _ J=0$, and hence $\mathrm d\Theta _ J=\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\Theta _ J=0$, where $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ is the operator ( 5.2.10 ). By the Leibniz rule for currents (section 5.3 ), $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\Theta _ J\wedge \sigma ^ m)=\Theta _ J\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\sigma ^ m)$. Since the closed $(1,1)$-form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q$ satisfies $\partial \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q= ar\partial \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=0$, we have $\mathrm d\sigma =\mathrm d\omega $, $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\sigma =\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sigma =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $, and the Leibniz rule gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\sigma ^ m)=m\, \sigma ^{m-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega +m(m-1)\, \sigma ^{m-2}\wedge \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega .  \] Expand $T_{\hat\imath }$ and $T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}$ in the same way. For a fixed $J$, with $m=n-1-|J|$, there are $m$ indices $i
otin J$ and $m(m-1)/2$ pairs $i<i'$ outside $J$; comparing coefficients, we obtain 0D9ABE7F6E36 10.9.7  egin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=\sum _ i\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge T_{\hat\imath } +2\sum _{i<i'}\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}. \end{equation} In particular $\mathrm dT=\sum _ J\Theta _ J\wedge \mathrm d(\sigma ^{n-1-|J|})$, $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ are currents of order zero, being sums of Bedford–Taylor products multiplied by smooth forms. The form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $ is real of bidegree $(2,2)$. Since $\partial \omega $ and $ ar\partial \omega $ have odd degree, $\partial \omega \wedge \partial \omega = ar\partial \omega \wedge  ar\partial \omega =0$ and $ ar\partial \omega \wedge \partial \omega =-\partial \omega \wedge  ar\partial \omega $, so $\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega = rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\partial \omega \wedge  ar\partial \omega $ is real of bidegree $(3,3)$; these forms vanish if $n<2$ and $n<3$, respectively. We claim that there is $C$ such that $C\omega ^2\pm \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $ and $C\omega ^3\pm \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ are strongly positive at every point of $X$. Consider $\omega ^2$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $, with $n\geq 2$; the other case, with $n\geq 3$, is the same. Let $D$ be a coordinate ball whose closure lies in a chart, and let $\mathcal C$ be the cone of strongly positive $(2,2)$-forms on $\mathbb C^ n$. For $x\in \overline D$, a complex linear change of coordinates takes $\omega (x)$ to $ eta $; since such changes preserve strong positivity in both directions, they map the interior of $\mathcal C$ onto itself, and $ eta ^2$ is an interior point of $\mathcal C$ (proposition 5.3.2 ). Hence $\omega (x)^2$ lies in the interior of $\mathcal C$. As $x\mapsto \omega (x)^2$ is continuous, these forms make up a compact subset of the interior of $\mathcal C$, which has a positive distance $d_0$ from the closed complement of the interior, for a fixed norm on the real $(2,2)$-forms. The coefficients of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega $ are bounded on $\overline D$, so for $C$ large the forms $\omega (x)^2\pm C^{-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega (x)$ lie at distance less than $d_0$ from $\omega (x)^2$, hence in $\mathcal C$, for all $x\in \overline D$. Covering the compact manifold $X$ by finitely many such balls proves the claim. The currents $T_{\hat\imath }$ and $T_{\hat\imath \hat\imath '}$ are positive, so $-CT_{\hat\imath }\wedge \omega ^2\leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge T_{\hat\imath }\leq CT_{\hat\imath }\wedge \omega ^2$, and similarly for the terms with $\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $. A real measure $
u $ with $-\mu \leq 
u \leq \mu $ for a positive measure $\mu $ satisfies $|
u |\leq \mu $, so ( 10.9.6 ), with the constant $2C$, follows from ( 10.9.7 ). Step 2. A convex cutoff. Put $w=v-u$, a bounded Borel function on $X$. Fix a smooth increasing function $\lambda \colon \mathbb R	o [0,1]$ with $\lambda =0$ on $(-\infty ,0]$ and $\lambda =1$ on $[1,\infty )$, and for $\delta >0$ put $F_\delta (t)=\int _0^ t\lambda (s/\delta )\, \mathrm ds$. Then $F_\delta $ is smooth and convex, $F_\delta =0$ on $(-\infty ,0]$, $0\leq F_\delta '\leq 1$, and as $\delta \downarrow 0$ we have $F_\delta (t)	o t^+$ and $F_\delta '(t)	o \mathbf1_{(0,\infty )}(t)$ for every real $t$; indeed $|F_\delta (t)-t|\leq \delta $ for $t>0$. We shall prove that, for every $\delta >0$, E24490F72C36 10.9.8  egin{equation}  \int _ XF_\delta '(w)\, (\omega _ v-\omega _ u)\wedge T\leq \int _ XF_\delta (w)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T. \end{equation} Granting this, let $\delta \downarrow 0$. The integrands converge pointwise and boundedly to $\mathbf1_ E$ and to $(v-u)\mathbf1_ E$; note that $F_\delta '(0)=0$, so the first limit is the indicator of $\{ w>0\} =E$. Both measures have finite total variation, so dominated convergence turns ( 10.9.8 ) into ( 10.9.5 ). To prove ( 10.9.8 ), choose finitely many coordinate balls $B_ k$ covering $X$, smooth functions $q_ k$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q_ k\geq \omega $ on a neighborhood of $\overline{B_ k}$, and a smooth partition of unity $(\chi _ k)$ on $X$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ k\subset B_ k$ (proposition 5.2.6 ). Fix $k$, write $\sigma _ k=\omega -\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q_ k$, and choose an open set $\Omega _ k$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ k\subset \Omega _ k\Subset B_ k$. Convolution of $u+q_ k$ and $v+q_ k$ with radial mollifiers whose radii decrease to zero and are smaller than the distance from $\Omega _ k$ to $\partial B_ k$ gives smooth plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega _ k$, which we write as $u_ l+q_ k$ and $v_ l+q_ k$. They decrease to $u+q_ k$ and $v+q_ k$ as $l	o \infty $, by proposition 5.9.2 (2), and they take values in a fixed compact interval $[-M',M']$, because $u+q_ k\leq u_ l+q_ k\leq u_1+q_ k$ and similarly for $v$. Then $w_ l=v_ l-u_ l	o w$ pointwise on $\Omega _ k$, with $|w_ l|\leq 2M'$. The function $f=F_\delta (w_ l)$ is smooth on $\Omega _ k$, which contains the support of $\chi _ kT$, so the definition of derivatives of currents and the Leibniz rule give \[  \int f\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi _ kT)=\int \chi _ k\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f\wedge T,\qquad \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi _ kT)=\chi _ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T+\Lambda _ k,  \] where $\Lambda _ k=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ k\wedge T+\mathrm d\chi _ k\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}T-\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\chi _ k\wedge \mathrm dT$, and the chain rule gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f=F_\delta '(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ l+F_\delta ''(w_ l)\,  rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \partial w_ l\wedge  ar\partial w_ l.  \] The last term is a smooth strongly positive $(1,1)$-form, since $F_\delta ''\geq 0$, and $T$ is positive, so the product of this term with $\chi _ kT$ is a positive measure. Consequently A8D59EA33A3E 10.9.9  egin{equation}  \int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ l\wedge T\leq \int F_\delta (w_ l) igl (\chi _ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T+\Lambda _ k igr ). \end{equation} Now let $l	o \infty $. By Step 1, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ and $\Lambda _ k$ are measures of finite total variation, so the right side tends to $\int F_\delta (w)(\chi _ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T+\Lambda _ k)$ by dominated convergence. On the left, write $T=\sum _ J\Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}$ as in Step 1, with $q=q_ k$ and $m_ J=n-1-|J|$. The exterior product of the smooth form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)$ with $\Theta _ J$ is the Bedford–Taylor product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J$, by ( 7.2.3 ), so the left side of ( 10.9.9 ) is the sum over $J$ of \[  \int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}-\int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}.  \] Fix $J$ and consider the first integral; the second is treated in the same way. Let $\vartheta >0$. By the Weierstrass approximation theorem there is a real polynomial $P$ of one variable with $|F_\delta '-P|\leq \vartheta $ on $[-2M',2M']$. The weights $P(w_ l)=P igl ((v_ l+q_ k)-(u_ l+q_ k) igr )$ are polynomials in two decreasing sequences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega _ k$, so corollary 7.3.8 , applied on $\Omega _ k$ with the closed positive base current $\Theta _ J$ and the decreasing factors $v_ l+q_ k$, gives the weak convergence of $P(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J$ to $P(w)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J$, which we test with the smooth form $\chi _ k\sigma _ k^{m_ J}$ with compact support in $\Omega _ k$. On the other hand, by theorem 7.2.5 and theorem 5.3.7 , the total variations on $\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ k$ of the coefficient measures of the positive currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J$ are bounded uniformly in $l$, so replacing $F_\delta '(w_ l)$ by $P(w_ l)$, or $F_\delta '(w)$ by $P(w)$, changes the integrals by at most a constant times $\vartheta $, with a constant independent of $l$. As $\vartheta $ was arbitrary, \[  \int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w_ l)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}\longrightarrow \int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}.  \] By ( 10.9.2 ), $\omega _ v\wedge T=\sum _ J\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+q_ k)\wedge \Theta _ J\wedge \sigma _ k^{m_ J}+\sigma _ k\wedge T$ on $B_ k$, and similarly for $u$. Summing over $J$, we conclude that the left side of ( 10.9.9 ) tends to $\int \chi _ kF_\delta '(w)\, (\omega _ v-\omega _ u)\wedge T$. Finally we sum the limiting inequalities over $k$. Since $\sum _ k\chi _ k=1$, we have $\sum _ k\Lambda _ k=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T-\sum _ k\chi _ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0$, and ( 10.9.8 ) follows. $\square$

title: Proposition 10.9.10
section: 10.9 Global poles on compact complex manifolds
text: Proposition 10.9.10 . CB97B7394604 There are constants $s_0,C>0$, depending only on $(X,\omega )$, with the following property. Let $u,v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ be bounded with $\omega _ v\geq \tfrac 12\omega $, put $E=\{ u<v\} $, and suppose that $v-u\leq s$ on $E$ for some $s\in (0,s_0)$. Then \[  \int _ E\omega _ v^ n\leq (1+Cs)\int _ E\omega _ u^ n.  \] In particular $\int _ X\omega _ u^ n>0$ for every bounded $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. Proof. We replace the factors $\omega _ v$ of $\omega _ v^ n$ by $\omega _ u$ one at a time, using lemma 10.9.4 ; the errors are traces of products with fewer factors different from $\omega $, and Steps 1 and 2 bound them by multiples of $\int _ E\omega _ u^ n$. For a product $T$ of $n-1$ factors chosen among $\omega ,\omega _ u,\omega _ v$, let $\mathcal P(T)$ be the set of products obtained from $T$ by deleting one factor and inserting $\omega ^2$, or by deleting two factors and inserting $\omega ^3$. The right side of ( 10.9.6 ) has at most $n^2$ terms, each of which is an element of $\mathcal P(T)$, and $0<v-u\leq s$ on $E$. Hence lemma 10.9.4 gives 232AA283C364 10.9.11 \begin{equation}  \int _ E\omega _ v\wedge T-\int _ E\omega _ u\wedge T\leq s\, |\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T|(E)\leq sB\sum _{P\in \mathcal P(T)}\int _ EP, \end{equation} with a constant $B\geq 1$ depending only on $(X,\omega )$. Step 1. Pure traces. For $0\leq k\leq n$ put $a_ k=\int _ E\omega _ u^ k\wedge \omega ^{n-k}\geq 0$, and apply ( 10.9.11 ) to $T=\omega _ u^ k\wedge \omega ^{n-k-1}$, $0\leq k<n$. The function $2v$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, because $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(2v)=2\omega _ v-\omega \geq 0$, and it is bounded. Since the products are affine in each potential and $v=\frac12\cdot 0+\frac12\cdot 2v$, we have $\omega _ v\wedge T=\frac12\omega \wedge T+\frac12\omega _{2v}\wedge T$, and $\omega _{2v}\wedge T$ is positive by lemma 10.9.3 (2); hence $\int _ E\omega _ v\wedge T\geq \tfrac 12a_ k$. Moreover $\int _ E\omega _ u\wedge T=a_{k+1}$, and the elements of $\mathcal P(T)$ are among the products $\omega _ u^ h\wedge \omega ^{n-h}$ with $h\in \{ k-2,k-1,k\} $. Thus ( 10.9.11 ) gives 1C288D4819F2 10.9.12 \begin{equation}  \tfrac 12a_ k\leq a_{k+1}+sB\sum _{h=0}^ k a_ h, \qquad 0\leq k<n. \end{equation} Choose $s_0>0$ with $s_0B(n+1)4^ n\leq 1/4$; in particular $sB\leq 1$. We prove $a_ k\leq 4a_{k+1}$ for $0\leq k<n$ by induction on $k$. If it holds for all smaller indices, then $a_ h\leq 4^{k-h}a_ k$ for $h\leq k$, so $\sum _{h=0}^ ka_ h\leq (k+1)4^ ka_ k$, and the error term in ( 10.9.12 ) is at most $s_0B(n+1)4^ na_ k\leq \tfrac 14a_ k$. Hence $\tfrac 12a_ k\leq a_{k+1}+\tfrac 14a_ k$, that is, $a_ k\leq 4a_{k+1}$. Consequently \[  a_ k\leq 4^{n-k}a_ n,\qquad 0\leq k\leq n.  \] Step 2. Mixed traces. For $j,k\geq 0$ with $j+k\leq n$ put $a_{j,k}=\int _ E\omega _ u^ j\wedge \omega _ v^ k\wedge \omega ^{n-j-k}\geq 0$, so that $a_{j,0}=a_ j$. If $k\geq 1$, apply ( 10.9.11 ) to $T=\omega _ u^ j\wedge \omega _ v^{k-1}\wedge \omega ^{n-j-k}$. Then $\int _ E\omega _ v\wedge T=a_{j,k}$ and $\int _ E\omega _ u\wedge T=a_{j+1,k-1}$, while every element of $\mathcal P(T)$ has fewer than $j+k$ factors different from $\omega $. Thus \[  a_{j,k}\leq a_{j+1,k-1}+sB\sum _{p+q<j+k}a_{p,q}\qquad (k\geq 1).  \] We show by induction on $m=j+k$ that $a_{j,k}\leq C_ m\sum _{h=0}^ ma_ h$ with $C_ m$ depending only on $n$. For $k=0$ this holds with $C_ m=1$. For $k\geq 1$, since $sB\leq 1$, applying the last inequality $k$ times, which replaces the factors $\omega _ v$ one at a time by $\omega _ u$, gives \[  a_{j,k}\leq a_{j+k,0}+k\sum _{p+q<m}a_{p,q},  \] and by the induction hypothesis the last sum, which has at most $(m+1)^2$ terms, is at most a constant depending only on $n$ times $\sum _{h<m}a_ h$. Together with Step 1 this shows $a_{j,k}\leq C'_ na_ n$ for all $j,k$, where $C'_ n$ depends only on $n$. Step 3. Conclusion. By symmetry of the products, \[  \omega _ v^ n-\omega _ u^ n=\sum _{i=0}^{n-1}(\omega _ v-\omega _ u)\wedge \omega _ v^ i\wedge \omega _ u^{n-1-i},  \] since the sum telescopes. Apply ( 10.9.11 ) to each of the $n$ products $T=\omega _ v^ i\wedge \omega _ u^{n-1-i}$. The resulting error terms are $sB$ times sums of at most $n^2$ traces $a_{p,q}$, hence at most a constant times $sa_ n$ by Step 2. Since $a_ n=\int _ E\omega _ u^ n$, this proves $\int _ E\omega _ v^ n\leq (1+Cs)\int _ E\omega _ u^ n$ with $C$ depending only on $(X,\omega )$. Step 4. Positivity. Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ be bounded, put $c=\inf _ Xu$, fix $s\in (0,s_0)$, and apply the inequality to the constant function $v=c+s$. Then $\omega _ v=\omega \geq \tfrac 12\omega $, and $E=\{ u<c+s\} $ is nonempty by the definition of the infimum and open because $u$ is upper semicontinuous; moreover $0<v-u\leq s$ on $E$ since $u\geq c$. Hence $0<\int _ E\omega ^ n\leq (1+Cs)\int _ E\omega _ u^ n$, and therefore $\int _ X\omega _ u^ n\geq \int _ E\omega _ u^ n>0$. $\square$

text: Lemma 10.9.13 . D94E16CFCA6C For every set $A\subset X$, exactly one of the following holds: $A$ is globally pluripolar, or $T_ A^*$ is a bounded nonnegative function in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. A subset of $X$ with nonempty interior is not globally pluripolar. A countable union of globally pluripolar sets is globally pluripolar. Proof. Let $\mathcal F_ A$ be the family of competitors for $T_ A$. It contains the constant $0$, so $T_ A\geq 0$. We first show that if $\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $\sup _ X\psi _ j=0$ for $j\geq 1$, then $\Psi =\sum _{j\geq 1}2^{-j}\psi _ j$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. By lemma 10.9.3 (4), there is a constant $M$ with $\| \psi _ j\| _{L^1(X)}\leq M$ for all $j$. The partial sums $\Psi _ N=\sum _{j=1}^ N2^{-j}\psi _ j$ decrease with $N$, since $\psi _ j\leq 0$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Psi _ N\geq -\sum _ j2^{-j}\omega \geq -\omega $. On a coordinate ball with a function $q$ as in ( 10.9.2 ), the functions $\Psi _ N+q$ are plurisubharmonic and decrease, so by theorem 5.10.1 their limit $\Psi +q$ is plurisubharmonic or identically $-\infty $ on the ball. By monotone convergence $\Psi _ N\to \Psi $ in $L^1(X)$ and $\int _ X|\Psi |\, \omega ^ n\leq \sum _ j2^{-j}M\leq M$, so $\Psi $ is finite almost everywhere and $\Psi +q$ is not identically $-\infty $ on any ball. Hence $\Psi $ is quasi-plurisubharmonic, and $\Psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ because the inequality $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Psi _ N\geq 0$ passes to the limit. Suppose now that $\sup \{ \sup _ Xu:u\in \mathcal F_ A\} =\infty $. Choose $u_ j\in \mathcal F_ A$ with $b_ j=\sup _ Xu_ j\geq 2^ j$ for $j\geq 1$, and put $\psi _ j=u_ j-b_ j$. Then $\psi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, $\sup _ X\psi _ j=0$ and $\psi _ j\leq -2^ j$ on $A$, so $\Psi =\sum _ j2^{-j}\psi _ j$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. Moreover $\Psi =-\infty $ on $A$, because every term $2^{-j}\psi _ j$ is at most $-1$ there and all terms are nonpositive. Thus $A$ is globally pluripolar. Otherwise $T_ A\leq C$ for a constant $C$, and by lemma 10.9.3 (1) the regularization $T_ A^*$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and satisfies $0\leq T_ A^*\leq C$. Thus at least one of the alternatives holds. They exclude each other: if $A\subset \{ \Phi =-\infty \} $ for a quasi-plurisubharmonic $\Phi $, choose $t>0$ with $t\Phi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$; then $t\Phi +c\in \mathcal F_ A$, hence $T_ A\geq t\Phi +c$, for every real $c$, so $T_ A^*$ is not bounded. A quasi-plurisubharmonic function is locally integrable (lemma 6.14.4 (1)), so its pole set has Lebesgue measure zero in every chart and contains no nonempty open set. Therefore a set with nonempty interior is not globally pluripolar. Finally let $A_ j\subset \{ \varphi _ j=-\infty \} $, $j\geq 1$, with $\varphi _ j$ quasi-plurisubharmonic. After multiplying by small positive constants and subtracting constants, we may assume that $\varphi _ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $\sup _ X\varphi _ j=0$. By the claim proved at the start, $\sum _ j2^{-j}\varphi _ j$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$; it equals $-\infty $ on every $A_ j$, because one term is $-\infty $ there and all terms are nonpositive. (A finite union is the case in which $A_ j=\varnothing $ for all large $j$.) $\square$

title: Lemma 10.9.15
section: 10.9 Global poles on compact complex manifolds
text: Lemma 10.9.15 . 29371C8618C2 Let $U,V$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a ball $B(a,r)\subset \mathbb C^ n$, $n\geq 1$, with $|V-U|\leq \kappa r^2$ for some $\kappa \geq 0$. Put $A=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}U$ and $D=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$. For every integer $0\leq k\leq n$, \[  \int _{B(a,r/2)}\sum _{j=0}^ k A^ j\wedge D^{k-j}\wedge \beta ^{n-k} \leq C_ n\sum _{l=0}^ k \kappa ^{k-l} \int _{B(a,r)}A^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l},  \] where $C_ n$ depends only on $n$ and $\kappa ^0=1$, also when $\kappa =0$. Proof. Put $\rho _ i=r/2+ir/(2n)$ and $B_ i=B(a,\rho _ i)$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, so that $B_0=B(a,r/2)$ and $B_ n=B(a,r)$. For $0\leq i<n$ fix a smooth function $\eta _ i\colon \mathbb R\to [0,1]$ with $\eta _ i=1$ on $(-\infty ,(\rho _ i/r)^2]$ and $\eta _ i=0$ on $[((\rho _ i+\rho _{i+1})/(2r))^2,\infty )$; the numbers $\rho _ i/r$ depend only on $n$ and $i$, so $\eta _ i$ can be chosen depending only on $n$ and $i$. By ( 10.9.14 ), the functions $\chi _ i(z)=\eta _ i(|z-a|^2/r^2)$ satisfy $\chi _ i\in C^\infty _ c(B_{i+1})$, $0\leq \chi _ i\leq 1$, $\chi _ i=1$ on $B_ i$ and $-C'r^{-2}\beta \leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ i\leq C'r^{-2}\beta $, where $C'=\max _ iC_{\eta _ i}$ depends only on $n$. For integers $j,m\geq 0$ with $j+m\leq n$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, put \[  I_ i(j,m)=\int _{B_ i}A^ j\wedge D^ m\wedge \beta ^{n-j-m}.  \] Let $m\geq 1$, $i<n$, and let $R=A^ j\wedge D^{m-1}\wedge \beta ^{n-j-m}$, a closed positive current by proposition 7.2.2 . By the definition and the symmetry of Bedford–Taylor products, $D\wedge R=A^ j\wedge D^ m\wedge \beta ^{n-j-m}$ and $D\wedge R-A\wedge R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}((V-U)R)$, so \[  \int \chi _ i\, D\wedge R=\int \chi _ i\, A\wedge R+\int (V-U)\, R\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ i.  \] Since $R$ is positive, the forms $C'r^{-2}\beta \pm \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ i$ give positive measures $R\wedge (C'r^{-2}\beta \pm \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi _ i)$; as $|V-U|\leq \kappa r^2$ and $\operatorname{Supp}\chi _ i\subset B_{i+1}$, the last integral is at most $C'\kappa \int _{B_{i+1}}R\wedge \beta $ in absolute value. Using $\mathbf1_{B_ i}\leq \chi _ i\leq \mathbf1_{B_{i+1}}$ and the positivity of the currents involved, we obtain \[  I_ i(j,m)\leq I_{i+1}(j+1,m-1)+C'\kappa \, I_{i+1}(j,m-1).  \] Both terms on the right have one factor $D$ fewer. Applying this inequality $m$ times, starting from $i=0$, we find \[  I_0(j,m)\leq \sum _{t=0}^ m\binom mt(C'\kappa )^{m-t}I_ m(j+t,0) \leq \sum _{t=0}^ m\binom mt(C'\kappa )^{m-t}\int _{B(a,r)}A^{j+t}\wedge \beta ^{n-j-t}.  \] Take $m=k-j$ and sum over $0\leq j\leq k$. With $l=j+t$ we have $m-t=k-l$, so every term with $A^ l$ carries the factor $\kappa ^{k-l}$, and the coefficients depend only on $n$. This proves the lemma; for $l=k$ the factor is $\kappa ^0=1$. $\square$

title: Proposition 10.9.16
section: 10.9 Global poles on compact complex manifolds
text: Proposition 10.9.16 . A3F29E1887A0 Let $K\subset X$ be compact, and suppose that $u=T_ K^*$ is bounded. Then the measure $\omega _ u^ n$ is carried by $K$. Moreover, with $S=\max \{ 1,\sup _ Xu\} $, 736BC1D7B247 10.9.17 \begin{equation}  0<\int _ X\omega _ u^ n\leq S^ n c_\omega (K). \end{equation} Proof. Steps 1–4 show that $\omega _ u^ n$ vanishes on $X\setminus K$: on small balls outside $K$ we compare $u$ with a homogeneous balayage computed with the coefficients of $\omega $ frozen. Step 5 proves the mass bound. Step 1. Increasing competitors. The competitors for $T_ K$ are bounded above by $\sup _ Xu$, and $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ by lemma 10.9.3 (1). Cover $X$ by finitely many coordinate charts. Applying Choquet's lemma (lemma 3.4.22 ) in each chart, we obtain for each chart a countable family of competitors whose supremum has, on that chart, the same upper semicontinuous regularization as $T_ K$. Let $v_1,v_2,\ldots $ be an enumeration of the union of these families. On each chart, $\sup _ kv_ k$ lies between the supremum of the family chosen for that chart and $T_ K$; since the regularization is computed locally, $(\sup _ kv_ k)^*=u$. The functions $u_ j=\max \{ 0,v_1,\ldots ,v_ j\} $ belong to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ by lemma 10.9.3 (1), increase with $j$, vanish on $K$, and are competitors; hence $0\leq u_ j\leq T_ K\leq u$, and $(\sup _ ju_ j)^*=u$, because $\sup _ kv_ k\leq \sup _ ju_ j\leq T_ K$. Step 2. Frozen balayage. Let $G\subset X\setminus K$ be the domain of a coordinate chart, identified with an open subset of $\mathbb C^ n$, and let $L\subset G$ be compact. Since $X\setminus K$ is open in the compact manifold $X$, it is a countable union of such sets $L$, so it suffices to show that $\omega _ u^ n(L)=0$. Choose open sets $G_2\Subset G_1\Subset G_0\Subset G$ with $L\subset G_2$. For $a\in G_2$ let $h_ a$ be the real quadratic polynomial with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h_ a=\omega (a)$ described at the beginning of this section. Choose $r_0>0$ with $2r_0<\operatorname {dist}(G_2,\mathbb C^ n\setminus G_1)$. The coefficients of $\omega $ have bounded first derivatives on $G_1$, so by the mean value inequality on balls there is $C_1$ such that, for $a\in G_2$ and $0<r\leq r_0$, the ball $B(a,2r)$ lies in $G_1$ and \[  -\delta \beta \leq \omega -\omega (a)\leq \delta \beta \quad \text{on }B(a,2r),\qquad \delta =C_1r;  \] indeed a Hermitian matrix whose entries are bounded by $\tau $ lies between $-n\tau $ and $n\tau $ times the identity. Fix such $a$ and $r$, put $q=\pi |z-a|^2$, so that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=\beta $ by ( 5.2.9 ), and let $B=B(a,r)$. The functions \[  U_ j=u_ j+h_ a+\delta q  \] are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B(a,2r)$, since they are quasi-plurisubharmonic and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}U_ j=\omega _{u_ j}+(\omega (a)-\omega +\delta \beta )\geq 0$. Let $V_ j$ be the homogeneous balayage of $U_ j$ in $B$ given by corollary 7.7.5 , applied on $B(a,2r)$: it equals $U_ j$ outside $B$, satisfies $V_ j\geq U_ j$ and $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_ j)^ n=0$ in $B$, and its restriction to $B$, being a member of the family described there, has upper boundary limits at most $U_ j$ on $\partial B$. We compare $V_ j$ with $u$. Put $\rho =q-\pi r^2$, which is nonpositive on $B$ and vanishes on $\partial B$, and let $Z_ j=V_ j-h_ a-\delta q+2\delta \rho $ on $B$. Then $Z_ j$ is quasi-plurisubharmonic and \[  \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}Z_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V_ j+(\omega -\omega (a)+\delta \beta )\geq 0,  \] so $Z_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(B,\omega )$, and for $x\in \partial B$ we have $\varlimsup _{B\ni y\to x}Z_ j(y)\leq U_ j(x)-h_ a(x)-\delta q(x)=u_ j(x)$. By lemma 10.9.3 (1), the function equal to $\max \{ u_ j,Z_ j\} $ on $B$ and to $u_ j$ on $X\setminus B$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$. It vanishes on $K$, because $B\cap K=\varnothing $, so it is a competitor for $T_ K$; hence $\max \{ u_ j,Z_ j\} \leq T_ K\leq u$ on $B$. Therefore \[  U_ j\leq V_ j\leq u+h_ a+\delta q-2\delta \rho \quad \text{on }B.  \] The balayage is increasing in the data, so $V_ j$ increases with $j$. Let $V$ be the upper semicontinuous regularization of $\lim _ jV_ j$ on $B$. Since $U_1\leq V_ j\leq u+h_ a+\delta q+2\pi \delta r^2$, the $V_ j$ are uniformly bounded, $V$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic, and $V_ j\to V$ almost everywhere by theorem 5.10.2 ; hence $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V)^ n=0$ on $B$ by theorem 7.6.1 . Put $U=u+h_ a+\delta q$. Since $\sup _ jU_ j=\sup _ ju_ j+h_ a+\delta q$, $h_ a+\delta q$ is continuous and $(\sup _ ju_ j)^*=u$, upper regularization gives $V\geq (\sup _ jU_ j)^*=U$. The upper bound for $V_ j$ is upper semicontinuous, so it also holds for $V$. As $-2\delta \rho \leq 2\pi \delta r^2$ on $B$, we conclude 435DB3D5519B 10.9.18 \begin{equation}  0\leq V-U\leq 2\pi \delta r^2\quad \text{on }B. \end{equation} Step 3. A local mass estimate. Put $A=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}U$ and $D=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ on $B$. The function $g=h_ a+\delta q$ satisfies $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g=\omega (a)+\delta \beta \geq \omega $ on $B(a,2r)$, so lemma 10.9.3 (2) gives $A^ n=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+g))^ n\geq \omega _ u^ n$ on $B$. By ( 10.9.14 ), with a fixed function $\eta $ equal to $1$ on $(-\infty ,1/16]$ and to $0$ on $[1/5,\infty )$, there is $\chi \in C^\infty _ c(B(a,r/2))$ with $0\leq \chi \leq 1$, $\chi =1$ on $B(a,r/4)$ and $-C_2r^{-2}\beta \leq \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \leq C_2r^{-2}\beta $, where $C_2$ does not depend on $a$ and $r$. By the definition and the symmetry of Bedford–Taylor products, $A^ n-D^ n=\sum _{j=0}^{n-1}(A-D)\wedge A^ j\wedge D^{n-1-j}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\bigl ((U-V)\sum _{j=0}^{n-1}A^ j\wedge D^{n-1-j}\bigr )$. Using $D^ n=0$, integration by parts against $\chi $, the positivity of the currents $A^ j\wedge D^{n-1-j}$ and ( 10.9.18 ), we obtain \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{B(a,r/4)}\omega _ u^ n & \leq \int \chi A^ n =\int (U-V)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \wedge \sum _{j=0}^{n-1}A^ j\wedge D^{n-1-j}\\ & \leq 2\pi C_2\delta \int _{B(a,r/2)} \sum _{j=0}^{n-1}A^ j\wedge D^{n-1-j}\wedge \beta . \end{aligned}  \] Apply lemma 10.9.15 with $k=n-1$ and $\kappa =2\pi \delta =2\pi C_1r$; for $r\leq 1/(2\pi C_1)$ we have $\kappa \leq 1$, and the last integral is at most $C_ n\sum _{l=0}^{n-1}\int _{B(a,r)}A^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l}$. To sum these estimates we replace $A$ by a current that does not depend on $a$ and $r$. Choose $C_0$ such that $C_0\beta \geq \omega $ on $G_0$ and $C_0\beta \geq \omega (a)+\delta \beta $ for all $a\in G_2$ and $r\leq r_0$. Then $\Gamma =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u+C_0\beta =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+C_0\pi |z|^2)$, where $u+C_0\pi |z|^2$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic on $G_0$ because $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+C_0\pi |z|^2)=\omega _ u+(C_0\beta -\omega )\geq 0$. On $B$ the difference $\Gamma -A$ is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ of the smooth function $C_0\pi |z|^2-h_ a-\delta q$, and it equals the form $\gamma =C_0\beta -\omega (a)-\delta \beta \geq 0$ with constant coefficients. By ( 10.9.1 ), $\Gamma ^ l=\sum _{i=0}^ l\binom liA^ i\wedge \gamma ^{l-i}$, and all terms are positive currents, so $A^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l}\leq \Gamma ^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l}$. Altogether, for $a\in G_2$ and $r\leq \min \{ r_0,1/(2\pi C_1)\} $, \[  \int _{B(a,r/4)}\omega _ u^ n\leq C_3\, r\sum _{l=0}^{n-1}\int _{B(a,r)}\Gamma ^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l},  \] with $C_3=2\pi C_1C_2C_ n$ independent of $a$ and $r$. Step 4. Zero mass off $K$. Let $r$ be as above and also smaller than $4\operatorname {dist}(L,\mathbb C^ n\setminus G_2)$, and consider the cubical grid $h\mathbb Z^{2n}\subset \mathbb C^ n=\mathbb R^{2n}$ of mesh $h=r/(4\sqrt{2n})$. The grid points $a$ within distance $r/4$ of $L$ are finitely many and belong to $G_2$. Every point of $\mathbb C^ n$ lies within distance $\sqrt{2n}\, h/2=r/8$ of a grid point, so the balls $B(a,r/4)$ centered at these grid points cover $L$. The centers of the balls $B(a,r)$ containing a given point $x$ lie in the cube of side $2r$ centered at $x$, which contains at most $(2r/h+1)^{2n}=(8\sqrt{2n}+1)^{2n}=N_ n$ grid points; so each point lies in at most $N_ n$ of these balls. Summing the local estimate over these balls, which lie in $G_1$, gives \[  \omega _ u^ n(L)\leq C_3N_ n\, r\sum _{l=0}^{n-1}\int _{\overline{G_1}}\Gamma ^ l\wedge \beta ^{n-l}.  \] The integrals on the right are finite by theorem 7.2.5 , applied in $G_0$, and do not depend on $r$. Letting $r\downarrow 0$ gives $\omega _ u^ n(L)=0$. Hence $\omega _ u^ n$ is carried by $K$. Step 5. The mass bound. Since $T_ K\geq 0$, we have $0\leq u\leq S$. The function $v=u/S$ satisfies $0\leq v\leq 1$ and belongs to $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ because $S\geq 1$: indeed $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v=S^{-1}\omega _ u+(1-S^{-1})\omega \geq 0$. Since $v=S^{-1}u+(1-S^{-1})\cdot 0$ and the products are affine in each potential, expanding $\omega _ v^ n$ factor by factor gives $\omega _ v^ n=\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nkS^{-k}(1-S^{-1})^{n-k}\omega _ u^ k\wedge \omega ^{n-k}$, and all terms are positive measures; hence $\omega _ v^ n\geq S^{-n}\omega _ u^ n$. As $\omega _ u^ n$ is carried by $K$, \[  \int _ X\omega _ u^ n=\int _ K\omega _ u^ n\leq S^ n\int _ K\omega _ v^ n\leq S^ nc_\omega (K).  \] Finally $\int _ X\omega _ u^ n>0$ by proposition 10.9.10 . $\square$

title: Theorem 10.9.19
section: 10.9 Global poles on compact complex manifolds
text: Theorem 10.9.19 . E2AF1B6D37EC Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, and let $A\subset X$ be pluripolar (definition 5.47.2 ). Then there is a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\Phi $ on $X$ with $A\subset \{ \Phi =-\infty \} $; that is, $A$ is globally pluripolar. Proof. The compact manifold $X$ has finitely many connected components, which are open, and it suffices to construct $\Phi $ on each of them, since the intersection of $A$ with a component is pluripolar in that component. On a component of dimension zero, which is a point, pluripolar sets are empty and $\Phi =0$ works. We may therefore assume that $X$ is connected of dimension $n\geq 1$, and we fix a Hermitian form $\omega $ on $X$ (one exists by section 5.6 ), so that the notation of this section applies. Every point of $X$ has a coordinate ball $U$ and a plurisubharmonic function on $U$ whose pole set contains $A\cap U$, by definition 5.47.2 ; choose a smaller ball $U_1\Subset U$ around the point. By compactness finitely many of the balls $U_1$ cover $X$. By the last assertion of lemma 10.9.13 it therefore suffices to prove the following: if $U$ is a coordinate ball, $\varphi $ is plurisubharmonic on $U$ and $U_1\Subset U$ is a smaller ball, then $E=\{ \varphi =-\infty \} \cap U_1$ is globally pluripolar. If $E$ is empty, there is nothing to prove, so let $E\neq \varnothing $. Choose balls $U_1\Subset U_2\Subset U_3\Subset U$ and subtract a constant from $\varphi $ so that $\varphi \leq 0$ on $U_3$. Suppose, to reach a contradiction, that $E$ is not globally pluripolar. By lemma 10.9.13 , there is a constant $C$ with $0\leq T_ E^*\leq C$. From the extremal functions of compact sublevel sets of regularizations of $\varphi $, which have small capacity, we shall obtain a bounded function in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ with zero Monge–Ampère mass. Step 1. Sublevel sets and their extremal functions. Convolution with radial mollifiers of radii decreasing to zero and smaller than the distance from $U_2$ to $\partial U_3$ gives smooth plurisubharmonic functions $\varphi _ j$ on $U_2$ that decrease to $\varphi $ as $j\to \infty $, by proposition 5.9.2 (2). Since $\varphi \leq 0$ on $U_3$, we have $\varphi \leq \varphi _ j\leq 0$ on $U_2$, so $\| \varphi _ j\| _{L^1(U_2)}\leq \| \varphi \| _{L^1(U_2)}<\infty $. For integers $N,j\geq 1$ put \[  K_{j,N}=\{ \varphi _ j\leq -N\} \cap \overline{U_1},\qquad O_{j,N}=\{ \varphi _ j<-N\} \cap U_1.  \] Then $K_{j,N}$ is compact and contains the open set $O_{j,N}$. Fix $x_0\in E$. Since $\varphi _ j(x_0)\downarrow -\infty $, there is $j_0(N)$ such that $x_0\in O_{j,N}$ for $j\geq j_0(N)$; we choose $j_0(N)$ nondecreasing in $N$. For these $j$ the set $K_{j,N}$ has nonempty interior, so $u_{j,N}=T_{K_{j,N}}^*$ is a bounded nonnegative function in $\mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ by lemma 10.9.13 . Every competitor for $T_{K_{j,N}}$ is nonpositive on the open set $O_{j,N}$; hence so is $T_{K_{j,N}}$, and its upper semicontinuous regularization satisfies $u_{j,N}=0$ on $O_{j,N}$. For fixed $N$, the sets $K_{j,N}$ increase with $j$, because $\varphi _ j$ decreases. A competitor for $T_{K_{j+1,N}}$ is a competitor for $T_{K_{j,N}}$, so $u_{j,N}$ decreases with $j\geq j_0(N)$; let $u_ N$ be its limit. By lemma 10.9.3 (3), $u_ N\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$, and $0\leq u_ N\leq u_{j_0(N),N}$ is bounded. If $x\in U_1$ and $\varphi (x)<-N$, then $x\in O_{j,N}$ for all large $j$, so $u_ N(x)=0$. In particular $u_ N=0$ on $E$, so $u_ N$ is a competitor for $T_ E$, and \[  0\leq u_ N\leq T_ E^*\leq C.  \] For fixed $j$, the sets $K_{j,N}$ decrease as $N$ increases, so $u_{j,N}\leq u_{j,N+1}$ for $j\geq j_0(N+1)$; letting $j\to \infty $ gives $u_ N\leq u_{N+1}$. Let $u_\infty $ be the upper semicontinuous regularization of $\lim _ Nu_ N$. By lemma 10.9.3 (1), $u_\infty \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $0\leq u_\infty \leq C$. Step 2. Convergence of the masses. By lemma 10.9.3 (3), applied to the uniformly bounded decreasing sequence $(u_{j,N})_{j\geq j_0(N)}$ and to the uniformly bounded increasing sequence $(u_ N)_{N\geq 1}$, and testing the weak convergence with the constant function $1$ on the compact manifold $X$, we obtain \[  \int _ X\omega _{u_{j,N}}^ n\longrightarrow \int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\quad (j\to \infty ),\qquad \int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\longrightarrow \int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n\quad (N\to \infty ).  \] Moreover $\int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n>0$ by proposition 10.9.10 , since $u_\infty $ is bounded. Step 3. The capacity of $K_{j,N}$. Choose a smooth function $h$ on $U_2$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\geq \omega $ and $\sup _{U_2}|h|<\infty $, for instance a large multiple of $|z|^2$. If $v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and $0\leq v\leq 1$, then $v+h$ is plurisubharmonic on $U_2$ with $|v+h|\leq 1+\sup _{U_2}|h|$, and $\omega _ v^ n\leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+h))^ n$ on $U_2$ by lemma 10.9.3 (2). Since $K_{j,N}\subset \overline{U_1}$ and $-\varphi _ j\geq N$ on $K_{j,N}$, while $-\varphi _ j\geq 0$ on $U_2$, the weighted Chern–Levine–Nirenberg inequality (theorem 7.4.1 ), applied in $U_2$ to $\varphi _ j$, the compact set $\overline{U_1}$ and a compact neighborhood $L\subset U_2$ of $\overline{U_1}$, gives \[  \int _{K_{j,N}}\omega _ v^ n \leq \frac1N\int _{\overline{U_1}}(-\varphi _ j)\, (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v+h))^ n \leq \frac{C'}N.  \] The constant $C'$ depends on $\| \varphi _ j\| _{L^1(L)}\leq \| \varphi \| _{L^1(U_2)}$ and on the bound for $|v+h|$, but not on $v$, $j$ or $N$. Taking the supremum over $v$, we obtain $c_\omega (K_{j,N})\leq C'/N$. Step 4. Conclusion. By proposition 10.9.16 , \[  \int _ X\omega _{u_{j,N}}^ n\leq \max \{ 1,\sup _ Xu_{j,N}\} ^ n\, \frac{C'}N\qquad (j\geq j_0(N)).  \] For fixed $N$, the uniformly bounded functions $u_{j,N}$ decrease to $u_ N$, so $u_{j,N}\to u_ N$ in $L^1(X)$ by dominated convergence, and $\sup _ Xu_{j,N}\to \sup _ Xu_ N$ by lemma 10.9.3 (4). Letting $j\to \infty $ and using $u_ N\leq C$, we obtain $\int _ X\omega _{u_ N}^ n\leq \max \{ 1,C\} ^ nC'/N$. Letting $N\to \infty $ gives $\int _ X\omega _{u_\infty }^ n=0$, which contradicts Step 2. Hence $E$ is globally pluripolar, and the theorem is proved. $\square$

title: 13.1 Non-pluripolar products
section: 13.1 Non-pluripolar products
text: In section 7.1 we multiplied the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1,\ldots ,\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p$ of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions by the Bedford–Taylor recursion $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge T=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1T)$. The potentials that arise in global geometry are often unbounded: by corollary 10.2.19 , a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on a compact Kähler manifold is $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ with $\theta $ a smooth form and $\varphi $ quasi-plurisubharmonic, and $\varphi =-\infty $ wherever the current has a positive Lelong number, for instance along a hypersurface carrying a current of integration. Indeed, at a point where $\varphi $ is finite, the spherical means of a local potential are bounded below by its value at that point, so the Lelong number vanishes there by ( 6.7.8 ). For such potentials the recursion breaks down, since it multiplies the measure coefficients of a current by an unbounded function. In this chapter we construct a product for arbitrary plurisubharmonic potentials which keeps positivity, closedness, multilinearity and locality, at the price of ignoring everything that happens on pluripolar sets. The construction truncates the potentials and discards their poles. We replace each $u_ j$ by $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $, take the Bedford–Taylor product, and keep only its restriction to the set where all $u_ j>-k$, on which the truncated potentials coincide with the original ones. Since bounded products are local in the plurifine topology (theorem 5.47.22 ), the restrictions obtained for different $k$ are compatible and increase with $k$. Their limit is the non-pluripolar product $\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p\rangle $, which by construction gives no mass to pluripolar sets. Two phenomena without counterpart in the bounded theory appear. The limit may have infinite mass on compact sets (example 13.2.9 ). And the mass carried by the poles is lost: in degree one, $\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\rangle $ is the restriction of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ to $\{ u>-\infty \} $ (proposition 13.4.7 ), so the current of integration at a point of $\mathbb P^1$ has zero non-pluripolar product, and even a potential with zero Lelong numbers and trivial multiplier ideals can have zero non-pluripolar mass (example 13.4.11 ). When the local masses are finite, the product is a closed positive current (theorem 13.3.1 ). On a compact Kähler manifold $X$ the local masses are always finite: every tuple of closed positive $(1,1)$-currents has a non-pluripolar product, and its total mass is bounded by a cohomological quantity (theorem 13.5.4 ). The total mass is, however, no longer determined by the cohomology classes of the factors; it depends on the singularities of the potentials. The central result of the second half of the chapter is that it is monotone in the singularities: if $\theta $ is a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form, $\varphi ,\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$, and $\psi $ is more singular than $\varphi $ in the sense of definition 10.3.7 , then the mass of $\varphi $ is at least that of $\psi $ (theorem 13.8.7 ). When all potentials are locally bounded outside the closed pole set of a fixed quasi-plurisubharmonic function, this follows from Stokes' formula; arbitrary singularities are reduced to this case by an auxiliary potential on $X\times \mathbb P^ N$, whose total mass is an average of the masses along a segment of potentials. Along the way we prove that non-pluripolar products are lower semicontinuous under convergence in capacity, and continuous when no mass is lost in the limit (theorem 13.7.5 ). Monotonicity has several consequences that are used in the following constructions. Mixed masses do not change under bounded perturbations of the potentials, and in a big class the potentials with minimal singularities have the largest masses; these maximal masses define the positive intersection numbers and the volume of pseudo-effective classes. The full-mass classes and the comparison and domination principles at the end of the chapter are basic tools for the envelopes of section 16.10 , and the fiber formula of section 13.6 is used for relative energy in section 17.1 . Historical remarks and references for this chapter are collected in subsection 25.1.15 . Let $X$ be a complex manifold and let $\varphi _1,\ldots ,\varphi _ p\in \mathrm{PSH}(X)$. When the functions $\varphi _ i$ are smooth, the differential form 82D27D8CAD36 13.1.1 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p \end{equation} is defined by the usual calculus. A central problem in pluripotential theory is to extend this product to singular plurisubharmonic functions in a reasonable way. We use the non-pluripolar product. This construction, originating in the work of Bedford–Taylor and developed in the global setting by Guedj–Zeriahi and Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, has two features that are essential for us: it is defined for arbitrary quasi-plurisubharmonic singularities, and it satisfies the monotonicity theorem for non-pluripolar masses. These two properties make it possible to compare singularity types through Monge–Ampère mass. The chapter is organized as follows. We first recall the Bedford–Taylor product for locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions. We then introduce the non-pluripolar product and record its basic functorial and locality properties. After a short discussion of quasi-continuous functions and capacity, we prove the convergence and concentration results used later in the theory of envelopes. The key tools extracted from this chapter are the monotonicity theorem, semicontinuity theorem, the concentration theorem for envelopes and the domination principle.

title: 13.2 Truncation and plurifine locality
section: 13.2 Truncation and plurifine locality
text:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold of dimension $n\geq 1$, let $U\subset X$ be a coordinate domain, and fix an integer $1\leq p\leq n$. Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ be plurisubharmonic functions on $U$, and recall that $\{ u_ j=-\infty \} $ is the pole set of $u_ j$. For each integer $k\geq 1$ put \[   egin{gathered} u_{j,k}=\max \{ u_ j,-k\} ,\qquad O_ k= igcap _{j=1}^ p\{ u_ j>-k\} ,\ S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,k}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,k}. \end{gathered}  \] The functions $u_{j,k}$ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic, so the product in $S_ k$ is the Bedford–Taylor product of definition 7.2.1 , and multiplication by $\mathbf1_{O_ k}$ restricts its coefficient measures to $O_ k$, where every $u_{j,k}$ coincides with $u_ j$. By proposition 5.47.23 , the trace measures of the currents $S_ k$ increase with $k$ to a Borel measure $\mu $ for which every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero, but $\mu $ may be infinite on compact sets (example 13.2.9 below). The set $O_ k$ is Borel, because plurisubharmonic functions are upper semicontinuous, and it is plurifine open, because they are plurifine continuous; it need not be open in the ordinary topology. For instance, the countable set $A$ of points with rational coordinates in the unit disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb C$ is polar, each point $a$ being the pole of $\log |z-a|$, so by proposition 4.1.11 there is a finite positive measure $
u $ with compact support such that the fundamental potential $E_2*
u $ equals $-\infty $ on $A$. The function $u_1(z)=(E_2*
u )(z_1)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\mathbb C^ n$ by proposition 3.4.11 , proposition 5.9.3 , and its pole set contains the dense subset $A	imes \mathbb C^{n-1}$ of $\Delta 	imes \mathbb C^{n-1}$. For $p=1$ and large $k$, the set $O_ k\cap (\Delta 	imes \mathbb C^{n-1})$ is nonempty, because $E_2*
u $ is locally integrable, but it has empty interior, so $O_ k$ is not open. We shall often restrict positive currents to Borel sets such as $O_ k$, and we first note that this preserves positivity. Lemma 13.2.1 . 6632853A40C9 Let $R$ be a positive current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on an open set $W\subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $E\subset W$ be a Borel set. Then the current $\mathbf1_ ER$, obtained by multiplying the coefficient measures of $R$ by $\mathbf1_ E$, is positive. If $R$ is strongly positive, that is, $R(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every test form $\varphi $ that is weakly positive at every point, then so is $\mathbf1_ ER$. Proof. By theorem 5.3.7 , $R$ has measure coefficients. Let $\varphi $ be a test form of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$ that is strongly positive, respectively weakly positive, at every point. The complex measure $R\wedge \varphi $, whose integral against a test function $\chi $ is $R(\chi \varphi )$, defines a positive distribution, because $\chi \varphi $ has the same positivity as $\varphi $ whenever $\chi \geq 0$; by the uniqueness in theorem 2.5.6 , it is a positive measure. Hence $(\mathbf1_ ER)(\varphi )=(R\wedge \varphi )(E)\geq 0$. $\square$ The next lemma shows that local finiteness of $\mu $ is exactly what is needed for the currents $S_ k$ to converge. Lemma 13.2.2 . D59675D9F6D8 For $l\geq k$ the current $S_ l-S_ k$ is positive, and $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. The currents $S_ k$ converge weakly to a positive current $S$ if and only if E88E33ACAD5B 13.2.3  egin{equation}  \sup _ k\int _ K S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}<\infty \quad 	ext{for every compact set }K\subset U, \end{equation} where $ eta $ is the Euclidean Kähler form ( 5.2.8 ) of the coordinates. In that case $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$ for every $k$, the coefficient measures of $S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ in total variation on compact subsets of $U$, and the trace measure of $S$ is the measure $\mu $ above. Every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero for $\mu $ and for the total variations of the coefficient measures of $S$; consequently every plurifine open subset of $U$ is measurable for the completions of these measures. Moreover, if $E_ k\subset O_ k$ are Borel sets such that $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ almost everywhere for the trace measure of $S$, then the coefficient measures of $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ when integrated against any bounded Borel function with compact support in $U$. This is the case, in particular, if the sets $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus  igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Proof. Let $l\geq k$. By proposition 5.47.23 , the level-$l$ and level-$k$ Bedford–Taylor products have the same restriction to $O_ k$; since $O_ k\subset O_ l$, this is the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. Consequently $S_ l-S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ l\setminus O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,l}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,l}$, and this current is positive by lemma 13.2.1 . Suppose that ( 13.2.3 ) holds. The trace measures $S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and, by ( 13.2.3 ), converge to a locally finite measure. Hence the trace mass of the positive current $S_ l-S_ k$ on a compact set $K$ tends to zero as $k,l	o \infty $. By theorem 5.3.7 , the total variation on $K$ of each coefficient measure of $S_ l-S_ k$ is at most a fixed multiple of this trace mass. Therefore each coefficient measure of $S_ k$ is a Cauchy sequence in total variation on compact sets, and the limits are the coefficients of a current $S$, which is positive as a weak limit of positive currents. Conversely, suppose that $S_ k	o S$ weakly for a positive current $S$. For every smooth compactly supported $\chi \geq 0$, the numbers $\int \chi S_ k\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and converge to $\int \chi S\wedge  eta ^{n-p}$, which therefore bounds them; choosing $\chi =1$ on $K$ gives ( 13.2.3 ). Assume now that ( 13.2.3 ) holds. Letting $l	o \infty $ in $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ gives $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$. By the convergence in total variation, the trace measure of $S$ is the increasing limit of the trace measures of the $S_ k$, which is $\mu $. By proposition 5.47.23 , every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer $\mu $-measure zero. The total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is at most $C_{n,p}\mu $ (theorem 5.3.7 ), so pluripolar sets have outer measure zero for these total variations as well, and theorem 5.47.20 (2), applied to $\mu $ and to these total variations, shows that plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for their completions. In particular $S$ vanishes on $U\setminus  igcup _ kO_ k$, the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, which is a pluripolar Borel set. Finally, let $E_ k$ be as in the statement. Since $E_ k\subset O_ k$, we have $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k=\mathbf1_{E_ k}S$. By theorem 5.3.7 , the total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is locally finite and absolutely continuous with respect to the trace measure. Hence $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ almost everywhere for each of these variations, and dominated convergence proves the assertion. If the $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus  igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar, then $\mathbf1_{E_ k}	o 1$ outside this pluripolar Borel set, which $S$ does not charge. $\square$ Definition 13.2.4 . D79952D7E272 If ( 13.2.3 ) holds, we say that the non-pluripolar product of $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite , and we call the limit $S$ of lemma 13.2.2 the non-pluripolar product \[  \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle =S.  \] The angle brackets distinguish this construction from a product that retains mass on pluripolar sets. The empty product ($p=0$) is $1$. If all $u_ j$ are locally bounded, then every relatively compact open subset of $U$ is contained in $O_ k$ for large $k$. In this case the non-pluripolar product is locally finite and coincides with the Bedford–Taylor product, and we omit the brackets. Proposition 13.2.5 . 1FAE60CC76F9 Every locally finite non-pluripolar product $S$ is strongly positive: $S(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every compactly supported smooth weakly positive form $\varphi $ of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$. Proof. First let all potentials be locally bounded. Near each point they are limits of decreasing sequences of smooth plurisubharmonic functions, for instance of their mollifications (proposition 5.9.2 (2)). The complex Hessians of these functions are semipositive $(1,1)$-forms (proposition 5.9.2 (1)), hence strongly positive, since the two notions of positivity coincide in bidegree $(1,1)$; by proposition 5.3.2 , their exterior products are strongly positive, and the product of such a product with a weakly positive form of complementary bidegree is a nonnegative multiple of the volume form. Thus the smooth products pair nonnegatively with every smooth compactly supported weakly positive form. By theorem 7.3.7 , the Bedford–Taylor product is their weak limit, and therefore it pairs nonnegatively with these forms as well. By lemma 13.2.1 , applied to the bounded products in the definition of $S_ k$, every $S_ k$ is strongly positive. Since $S_ k	o S$ weakly by lemma 13.2.2 , so is $S$. $\square$ Proposition 13.2.6 . 7F7123F92478 Let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ p$ and $v_1,\ldots ,v_ p$ be plurisubharmonic on $U$. If $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$, then the non-pluripolar product of the $u_ j$ is locally finite if and only if that of the $v_ j$ is, and then the two products are equal; thus local finiteness and the product depend only on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. The product is symmetric in its factors and local in the plurifine topology: if $u_ j=v_ j$ on a plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$ and both products are locally finite, then they have the same restriction to $O$. Finally, the product is multilinear: if $u_1'$ is plurisubharmonic on $U$, then the product of $u_1+u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite if and only if the products of $u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ and of $u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ are, and in that case \[   egin{aligned}  \langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1+u_1')\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle & =\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle \ & \quad +\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1'\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle . \end{aligned}  \] Similarly, for real $c>0$ the product of $cu_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is locally finite if and only if that of $u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$ is, and then it is $c$ times the latter. Proof. In this proof we write $P^{(m)}(w_1,\ldots ,w_ p)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_1,-m\} \wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ w_ p,-m\} $ for plurisubharmonic $w_1,\ldots ,w_ p$ and an integer $m\geq 1$. Symmetry and locality. Each truncated product $S_ k$ is symmetric in its factors, hence so is the limit. Suppose that $u_ j=v_ j$ on the plurifine open set $O$ for every $j$, and that both products are locally finite. By lemma 13.2.2 , plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for the completions of the total variations of the coefficient measures of both products, so the restrictions of the products to $O$ and to the plurifine open sets $W_ k=O\cap  igcap _ j\{ u_ j>-k\} =O\cap  igcap _ j\{ v_ j>-k\} $ are well defined; the sets $W_ k$ increase with $k$. On $W_ k$ the truncations $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ coincide, so the two level-$k$ products agree on $W_ k$ by theorem 5.47.22 . Since $W_ k$ is contained in the level-$k$ sets of both tuples, lemma 13.2.2 shows that the two non-pluripolar products also agree on $W_ k$. The union of the $W_ k$ is $O$ minus the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, a pluripolar set, which has outer measure zero for these total variations by the same lemma. Letting $k	o \infty $, we conclude that the two products have the same restriction to $O$. Dependence on the currents $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$. Suppose that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j$ for every $j$. The distribution $v_ j-u_ j$ then has zero Laplacian, so by Weyl's lemma (theorem 3.1.11 ) it is a smooth function $w_ j$, and its complex Hessian vanishes: $w_ j$ is pluriharmonic. The plurisubharmonic functions $v_ j$ and $u_ j+w_ j$ agree almost everywhere, hence everywhere, since both are subharmonic (theorem 5.9.1 , theorem 3.4.12 ). Fix a relatively compact open set $V\subset U$ and an integer $C$ such that $|w_ j|\leq C$ on $V$ for all $j$. Write $O_ k(u),S_ k(u)$ and $O_ k(v),S_ k(v)$ for the level sets and truncated products of the two tuples. On $V\cap O_ k(v)$ we have $u_ j=v_ j-w_ j>-k-C$, hence \[  \max \{ v_ j,-k\} =v_ j=\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j .  \] The functions $\max \{ v_ j,-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-k-C\} +w_ j$ are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $V$ and coincide on $V\cap O_ k(v)$. Moreover, adding the pluriharmonic function $w_ j$ to a factor does not change Bedford–Taylor products. Indeed, by additivity (proposition 7.2.2 ) and symmetry (theorem 7.3.7 ), the difference is a sum of products having $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j$ as first factor; by proposition 7.2.2 (1), such a product is the exterior product of the remaining closed positive current with the smooth form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ j=0$. As $V\cap O_ k(v)\subset O_{k+C}(u)$, plurifine locality gives on $V$ \[  S_ k(v)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}P^{(k+C)}(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)=\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}S_{k+C}(u)\leq S_{k+C}(u).  \] Thus ( 13.2.3 ) for the $u_ j$ implies ( 13.2.3 ) for the $v_ j$ on compact subsets of $V$, and exchanging the two tuples (that is, replacing $w_ j$ by $-w_ j$) gives the converse. If both products are locally finite, the display and lemma 13.2.2 give $\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ pangle =\mathbf1_{O_ k(v)}\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle $ on $V$ for every $k$. The sets $O_ k(v)$ exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets, which are the same for the two tuples and carry no mass for either product. Hence the two products coincide. Additivity. Let $u_1'$ be plurisubharmonic and put \[  E_ k=\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ u_1'>-k\}  \cap  igcap _{j=2}^ p\{ u_ j>-k\} .  \] These plurifine open sets increase with $k$ and exhaust the complement of the union of the pole sets of $u_1,u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p$. On $E_ k$ we have $\max \{ u_1+u_1',-2k\} =u_1+u_1'=\max \{ u_1,-k\} +\max \{ u_1',-k\} $ and $\max \{ u_ j,-2k\} =\max \{ u_ j,-k\} $ for $j\geq 2$. Plurifine locality and the additivity of bounded products (proposition 7.2.2 ) therefore give 491D0E94E07A 13.2.7  egin{equation}   egin{aligned}  \mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(2k)}(u_1+u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p) & =\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1,u_2,\ldots ,u_ p)\ & \quad +\mathbf1_{E_ k}P^{(k)}(u_1',u_2,\ldots ,u_ p). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Before local finiteness is known we argue with trace measures. By proposition 5.47.23 , for each of the three tuples the trace measures of the truncated products increase to a Borel measure, possibly infinite on compact sets, for which every pluripolar set has outer measure zero; for a locally finite product it is the trace measure of the product. The set $E_ k$ is contained in the level-$2k$ set of the first tuple and in the level-$k$ sets of the other two, so by the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ of lemma 13.2.2 , the restriction of each limit measure to $E_ k$ is the restriction of the corresponding trace measure in ( 13.2.7 ). Hence, on $E_ k$, the limit measure of the first tuple is the sum of those of the other two. Letting $k	o \infty $, monotone convergence gives this equality on every Borel subset of $ igcup _ kE_ k$, and hence everywhere, because the complement of $ igcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Since all three measures are positive, the first is locally finite if and only if the other two are; this is the asserted equivalence of local finiteness. When the products are locally finite, ( 13.2.7 ) and lemma 13.2.2 give the additivity identity on each $E_ k$, and letting $k	o \infty $ proves it. For $c>0$ the same argument applies to the sets $\{ u_1>-k\} \cap \{ cu_1>-k\} \cap  igcap _{j\geq 2}\{ u_ j>-k\} $, on which $\max \{ cu_1,-k\} =c\max \{ u_1,-k\} $, and proves the homogeneity assertion. $\square$ Let now $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on the complex manifold $X$. By theorem 5.4.3 , every point of $X$ has a coordinate neighborhood on which $T_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ with $u_ j$ plurisubharmonic. By proposition 13.2.6 , local finiteness and the local non-pluripolar product do not depend on the choice of these potentials, and the construction is compatible with restriction to smaller open sets. They do not depend on the coordinates either. Indeed, let $F$ be a biholomorphism between coordinate domains. Then $\max \{ u_ j,-k\} \circ F=\max \{ u_ j\circ F,-k\} $ and $O_ k(u\circ F)=F^{-1}(O_ k(u))$. Since $F$ is a submersion, the pullback $F^*$ of proposition 5.6.2 satisfies $F^*(\mathbf1_ ES)=\mathbf1_{F^{-1}(E)}F^*S$ for every current $S$ of order zero and every Borel set $E$ (corollary 5.6.4 (2)), so proposition 7.2.2 (5) gives $F^*S_ k(u)=S_ k(u\circ F)$ for the truncated products. To compare trace measures, note that if $\alpha $ and $\alpha '$ are smooth semipositive $(1,1)$-forms on an open set with $\alpha '\leq c\alpha $, then \[  (c\alpha )^{n-p}-\alpha '^{n-p}=(c\alpha -\alpha ')\wedge \sum _{i=0}^{n-p-1}(c\alpha )^ i\wedge \alpha '^{n-p-1-i}  \] is a sum of products of semipositive $(1,1)$-forms, hence strongly positive (proposition 5.3.2 ). Since the product of a positive current with a smooth strongly positive form of complementary bidegree is a positive measure, it follows that 591B39D2BEA0 13.2.8  egin{equation}  R\wedge \alpha '^{n-p}\leq c^{n-p}R\wedge \alpha ^{n-p} \end{equation} on that open set, for every positive current $R$ of bidegree $(p,p)$. On a neighborhood of a compact set, the Euclidean forms $ eta $ and $ eta '$ of the two coordinate systems satisfy $ eta '\leq c eta $ for some $c$ (lemma 6.14.1 ), so by ( 13.2.8 ) the trace measures of a positive current in the two coordinate systems are comparable on compact sets, and local finiteness does not depend on the coordinates. Since $F^*$ is weakly continuous, $F^*\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ pangle =\langle \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1\circ F)\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ p\circ F)angle $. We say that the non-pluripolar product of $T_1,\ldots ,T_ p$ is locally finite if this holds near every point; the local products then glue to a positive current $\langle T_1\wedge \cdots \wedge T_ pangle $ on $X$, which is closed by theorem 13.3.1 below. When $X$ is compact we also say simply that the product is finite . Repeated factors are written as powers, as in $\langle T^ j\wedge S^{r-j}angle $, and for $T_ j=	heta _ j+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ j$ we also write $\langle (	heta _1+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _1)\wedge \cdots \wedge (	heta _ p+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi _ p)angle $. The assertions of proposition 13.2.6 carry over to these products, with multilinearity in the factors $T_ j$. Example 13.2.9 . 6F4C920FEDCA Let $U=\{ (x,y)\in \mathbb C^2:|x|^2<1/2,\  |y|<\mathrm e^{-1}\} $, put $L=-\log |y|$, and define \[  u(x,y)=(|x|^2-1)\sqrt L\quad (y
e 0),\qquad u(x,0)=-\infty .  \] On $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $ we have $L>1$, the function $u$ is smooth, and its complex second derivatives are \[  u_{x ar x}=\sqrt L,\qquad u_{y ar y}= rac{1-|x|^2}{16|y|^2L^{3/2}},\qquad u_{x ar y}=- rac{ ar x}{4 ar y\sqrt L},\qquad \det (u_{j ar k})= rac{1-2|x|^2}{16|y|^2L}.  \] Since $u_{x ar x}>0$ and $\det (u_{j ar k})>0$, the complex Hessian is positive definite, so $u$ is plurisubharmonic off the axis $\{ y=0\} $ (proposition 5.9.2 (1)). Moreover $u<-\sqrt L/2$ is bounded above and tends to $-\infty $ at the axis. By theorem 5.11.1 , the plurisubharmonic extension across the axis takes the value $\varlimsup u=-\infty $ there, which is the displayed value; hence $u$ is plurisubharmonic on $U$. Off the axis, $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$ is the smooth measure with density a fixed positive multiple of $\det (u_{j ar k})$, by ( 7.2.4 ). The sets $O_ k=\{ u>-k\} $ are open, since $u$ is continuous as an extended-real function, and they increase to $U\setminus \{ y=0\} $; on $O_ k$ the truncation $\max \{ u,-k\} $ equals $u$, so $S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2$. Take $K=\{ |x|^2\leq 1/4,\  |y|\leq r\} $ with $0<r<\mathrm e^{-1}$. On $K$ we have $1-2|x|^2\geq 1/2$, and polar coordinates in $y$ give \[  \int _{|y|\leq r} rac{\mathrm dA(y)}{|y|^2L}=2\pi \int _0^ r rac{\mathrm dt}{t(-\log t)}=\infty .  \] Hence $\sup _ k\int _ KS_ k=\int _{K\setminus \{ y=0\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2=\infty $, and ( 13.2.3 ) fails. Thus the non-pluripolar product of an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function need not be locally finite.

title: Lemma 13.2.1
section: 13.2 Truncation and plurifine locality
text: Lemma 13.2.1 . 6632853A40C9 Let $R$ be a positive current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on an open set $W\subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $E\subset W$ be a Borel set. Then the current $\mathbf1_ ER$, obtained by multiplying the coefficient measures of $R$ by $\mathbf1_ E$, is positive. If $R$ is strongly positive, that is, $R(\varphi )\geq 0$ for every test form $\varphi $ that is weakly positive at every point, then so is $\mathbf1_ ER$. Proof. By theorem 5.3.7 , $R$ has measure coefficients. Let $\varphi $ be a test form of bidegree $(n-p,n-p)$ that is strongly positive, respectively weakly positive, at every point. The complex measure $R\wedge \varphi $, whose integral against a test function $\chi $ is $R(\chi \varphi )$, defines a positive distribution, because $\chi \varphi $ has the same positivity as $\varphi $ whenever $\chi \geq 0$; by the uniqueness in theorem 2.5.6 , it is a positive measure. Hence $(\mathbf1_ ER)(\varphi )=(R\wedge \varphi )(E)\geq 0$. $\square$

title: Lemma 13.2.2
section: 13.2 Truncation and plurifine locality
text: Lemma 13.2.2 . D59675D9F6D8 For $l\geq k$ the current $S_ l-S_ k$ is positive, and $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. The currents $S_ k$ converge weakly to a positive current $S$ if and only if E88E33ACAD5B 13.2.3 \begin{equation}  \sup _ k\int _ K S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}<\infty \quad \text{for every compact set }K\subset U, \end{equation} where $\beta $ is the Euclidean Kähler form ( 5.2.8 ) of the coordinates. In that case $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$ for every $k$, the coefficient measures of $S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ in total variation on compact subsets of $U$, and the trace measure of $S$ is the measure $\mu $ above. Every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer measure zero for $\mu $ and for the total variations of the coefficient measures of $S$; consequently every plurifine open subset of $U$ is measurable for the completions of these measures. Moreover, if $E_ k\subset O_ k$ are Borel sets such that $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ almost everywhere for the trace measure of $S$, then the coefficient measures of $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k$ converge to those of $S$ when integrated against any bounded Borel function with compact support in $U$. This is the case, in particular, if the sets $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus \bigcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar. Proof. Let $l\geq k$. By proposition 5.47.23 , the level-$l$ and level-$k$ Bedford–Taylor products have the same restriction to $O_ k$; since $O_ k\subset O_ l$, this is the identity $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$. Consequently $S_ l-S_ k=\mathbf1_{O_ l\setminus O_ k}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,l}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{p,l}$, and this current is positive by lemma 13.2.1 . Suppose that ( 13.2.3 ) holds. The trace measures $S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and, by ( 13.2.3 ), converge to a locally finite measure. Hence the trace mass of the positive current $S_ l-S_ k$ on a compact set $K$ tends to zero as $k,l\to \infty $. By theorem 5.3.7 , the total variation on $K$ of each coefficient measure of $S_ l-S_ k$ is at most a fixed multiple of this trace mass. Therefore each coefficient measure of $S_ k$ is a Cauchy sequence in total variation on compact sets, and the limits are the coefficients of a current $S$, which is positive as a weak limit of positive currents. Conversely, suppose that $S_ k\to S$ weakly for a positive current $S$. For every smooth compactly supported $\chi \geq 0$, the numbers $\int \chi S_ k\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$ increase with $k$ and converge to $\int \chi S\wedge \beta ^{n-p}$, which therefore bounds them; choosing $\chi =1$ on $K$ gives ( 13.2.3 ). Assume now that ( 13.2.3 ) holds. Letting $l\to \infty $ in $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S_ l=S_ k$ gives $\mathbf1_{O_ k}S=S_ k$. By the convergence in total variation, the trace measure of $S$ is the increasing limit of the trace measures of the $S_ k$, which is $\mu $. By proposition 5.47.23 , every pluripolar subset of $U$ has outer $\mu $-measure zero. The total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is at most $C_{n,p}\mu $ (theorem 5.3.7 ), so pluripolar sets have outer measure zero for these total variations as well, and theorem 5.47.20 (2), applied to $\mu $ and to these total variations, shows that plurifine open subsets of $U$ are measurable for their completions. In particular $S$ vanishes on $U\setminus \bigcup _ kO_ k$, the union of the pole sets of the $u_ j$, which is a pluripolar Borel set. Finally, let $E_ k$ be as in the statement. Since $E_ k\subset O_ k$, we have $\mathbf1_{E_ k}S_ k=\mathbf1_{E_ k}S$. By theorem 5.3.7 , the total variation of each coefficient measure of $S$ is locally finite and absolutely continuous with respect to the trace measure. Hence $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ almost everywhere for each of these variations, and dominated convergence proves the assertion. If the $E_ k$ increase and $U\setminus \bigcup _ kE_ k$ is pluripolar, then $\mathbf1_{E_ k}\to 1$ outside this pluripolar Borel set, which $S$ does not charge. $\square$
